note: 该谚语适用于非正式口语或书面劝诫，语气中性偏严肃，无冒犯性，用于提醒他人勿仓促结婚。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友在派对上认识了一个人，约会才两周就冲动决定领证结婚，完全没来得及了解对方的生活习惯、价值观和家庭情况。例句：My cousin married someone she'd only known for three months right after graduation, and now they're constantly fighting over money, household chores, and future plans—she really should have remembered that marry in haste, repent at leisure. 翻译：我表姐刚毕业就嫁给了一个只认识三个月的人，现在他们成天为了钱、家务和未来的计划吵架——她当初真该记住“草率结婚，事后后悔”这个道理。

word: May you live in interesting times
definitionCn: 愿你的生活充满混乱与烦恼。
englishDefinition: May you experience much disorder and trouble in your life.
example: When my boss said "May you live in interesting times" right before the company restructuring, I knew I was in for a rough few months.
exampleTranslation: 当我老板在公司重组前说“祝你生活在有趣的时代”时，我就知道接下来的几个月我要不好过了。
origin: 传为西方讹称的中国古诅咒，反讽“有趣时代”实为动荡多事之秋。
note: 反讽英式诅咒，口语非正式，带恶意贬义，用于嘲讽或咒人，正式场合禁用，避免对亲友使用。 场景考察：情景：你和朋友正在讨论最近接连发生的糟心事，朋友吐槽说“我最近真是水逆到不行，先是丢了钱包，接着又被公司裁员，连租的房子都突然要涨房租”，你可以用这句俚语回应他，调侃他当下的处境。 例句：My friend has been complaining about his terrible luck lately, and I joked that it seems like someone wished him "May you live in interesting times." 翻译：我的朋友最近一直在吐槽自己运气差到极点，我开玩笑说看来有人给他许下了“祝你生活在有趣的时代”的“祝福”。

definitionCn: 这是我的错。从拉丁语直译过来就是“因我自己的过错”。 即使是那些不会说拉丁语的人，大概也能猜到这个短语的意思是“我有罪”，或者诸如此类的意思。
englishDefinition: I'm to blame. The literal translation from the Latin is 'through my own fault'. Even those who don't speak Latin could probably make a guess that this phrase means 'I am culpable', or words to that effect.
example: Mea culpa — I should have double-checked the report before sending it out to the whole team.
exampleTranslation: 是我的错——我本该在把报告发给全团队之前再核对一遍的。
origin: 源自拉丁语，原意为“因我之过”，用于承认自身过错、承担责任。
note: Mea culpa是拉丁语借词，口语书面通用，表自责认错，中性偏正式，无褒贬，用于承认自身过错的场合。 场景考察：情景：你作为团队项目的负责人，因为自己漏发了关键的会议通知，导致整个小组错过了和导师的进度汇报，被导师批评后你主动向组员承认错误。 例句：Mea culpa — I forgot to send out the group meeting reminder, which made us miss the check-in with our advisor. 翻译：是我的错——我忘了发小组会议提醒，害得我们错过了和导师的进度汇报。

definitionCn: “一肉两菜”，即肉配土豆和另一种蔬菜，是一道传统的英式餐食。
englishDefinition: Meat and two vegetables, that is, meat with potatoes and another vegetable, is a traditional English meal.
example: On Sundays, my grandma always cooks a proper plate of meat and two veg for the whole family.
exampleTranslation: 每逢周日，我奶奶总会为全家人做一份地道的英式传统餐——肉配两样蔬菜。
origin: 源自英国传统家常正餐，指配土豆及另一蔬菜的肉菜组合，后成英式日常饮食代称。
note: 英式传统餐食俚语，口语非正式，中性无褒贬，日常饮食交流用，勿用于正式餐饮场合。 场景考察：情景：周末你和英国本地的房东一起在家吃午餐，房东端上了烤牛排、烤土豆和水煮西兰花，笑着跟你介绍这是最经典的英式家常餐食，你想用上刚学到的俚语回应房东，表达你对这道传统餐食的认可。 例句："This cozy Sunday lunch of roast beef, crispy roast potatoes and steamed greens is exactly the classic 'meat and two veg' I've been wanting to try since I arrived in the UK." 翻译：“这份有烤牛肉、香酥烤土豆和清炒时蔬的惬意周日午餐，正是我来到英国之后一直想尝尝的经典‘一荤两素’传统餐食。”

definitionCn: 进入最终决胜赛。
englishDefinition: Arrive at a final decisive contest.
example: After years of dominating the industry, the tech giant finally met its Waterloo when it failed to adapt to the shifting market demands.
exampleTranslation: 在主导行业多年后，这家科技巨头因未能适应不断变化的市场需求，最终遭遇了滑铁卢。
origin: 源自1815年滑铁卢战役，拿破仑战败，喻遭遇决定性失败。
note: 多用于口语，带戏谑或惋惜色彩，非正式场合使用，不宜对刚遭遇重大失败的人当面提及。 场景考察：情景：校队王牌前锋带领的高中篮球队一路连胜闯入州决赛，却遇到了防守体系滴水不漏的老牌劲旅，全场被压制最终输掉了冠军争夺战。 例句：After winning every regional match that season, the star high school basketball team met their Waterloo in the state final, where they were thoroughly outplayed by a defensive powerhouse. 翻译：在那个赛季赢下所有地区赛后，这支明星高中篮球队在州决赛中遭遇了滑铁卢，被一支防守强队彻底压制。

definitionCn: “柔黄”指的是被当作轻度麻醉品吸食（或被认为被吸食）的干香蕉皮。
englishDefinition: Mellow yellow describes dried banana skin that was smoked, or believed to be smoked, as a mild intoxicant.
example: Back in the 1960s, some people believed that smoking mellow yellow — dried banana skins — could give you a mild high.
exampleTranslation: 早在20世纪60年代，有些人相信吸食“黄香蕉”——晒干的香蕉皮——能带来轻微的迷幻感。
origin: 源自1960年代反主流文化，指吸食干燥香蕉皮以获得轻度迷幻体验的说法。
note: 俚语，口语非正式，中性偏戏谑，仅用于熟人闲聊，勿在正式场合或对陌生人使用。 场景考察：情景：一群大学生在宿舍里翻找旧物时，聊起上世纪60年代流行的各种新奇消遣方式，其中有人提到了一种传说中能带来轻微致幻效果的特殊烟料。 例句：Back in the 1960s, some people believed that mellow yellow — dried banana skins — could be smoked to produce a mild intoxicating effect. 翻译：早在20世纪60年代，有些人相信“黄香蕉”——晒干的香蕉皮——可以通过吸食来产生轻微的致幻效果。

definitionCn: 一个虚构的田园诗般的地方，人们在那里通过对过往经历的回忆进行感伤的旅行。 这个表达通常以其扩展形式使用——“a trip down memory lane”或“walk down memory lane”。
englishDefinition: An imaginary idyllic place where people take sentimental journeys through their memories of past experiences. The expression is often used in its extended forms - 'a trip down memory lane' or 'walk down memory lane'.
example: On our 20th high school reunion, we took a trip down memory lane, flipping through old yearbooks and laughing at the silly pranks we pulled back then.
exampleTranslation: 在高中毕业20周年聚会上，我们重温了往昔时光，翻看着旧年鉴，笑着聊起当年搞过的那些荒唐恶作剧。
origin: “Memory lane”指记忆中美好过往，“漫步记忆小径”喻怀旧之旅，源自对往昔的感性追忆。
note: 口语怀旧场景，褒义，用于亲友闲聊，不宜正式场合，礼貌温和，指追忆过往美好时光。 场景考察：情景：周末你整理旧储物箱时，翻出了小学毕业照、当年攒的球星卡和第一辆自行车的旧照片，忍不住坐在地板上一张张翻看，满脑子都是小时候和伙伴们疯玩的画面。 例句：Looking through my old childhood photo album on a rainy weekend took me right down memory lane. 翻译：在一个下雨的周末翻看我童年的旧相册，让我瞬间踏上了追忆往事的旅程。

definitionCn: 那些墨守成规、服从官方路线的商人、官僚、军人等诸如此类的人。也可直接称为“西装革履的人”。
englishDefinition: Businessmen/bureaucrats/soldiers and the like who follow convention and the company line. Also called just 'suits'.
example: The men in suits at headquarters rejected the grassroots proposal without even reading it.
exampleTranslation: 总部那些循规蹈矩的西装男甚至没读这份基层提案就直接否决了它。
origin: 源自职场着装文化，指穿西装的商人、官僚等循规蹈矩、服从上级的群体。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，略带贬义，指循规蹈矩、服从指令的商人、官僚或军人等。 场景考察：情景：在一家大型科技公司的季度战略会议上，一群身着正装的高管围坐在会议桌旁，讨论是否要推出一款打破行业常规的创新产品。例句：The men in suits at the headquarters rejected the young team's bold creative proposal, insisting that the company stick to its proven, traditional business model. 翻译：总部的那些西装革履的高管们否决了年轻团队大胆的创意提案，坚持要求公司沿用其成熟的传统商业模式。

word: Men's evil manners live in brass; their virtues we write in water
phonetic: /menz ˈiːvl ˈmænəz lɪv ɪn brɑːs ðeə ˈvɜːtʃuːz wiː raɪt ɪn ˈwɔːtə/
definitionCn: 我一直没法释怀之前的小组搭档抢了我的功劳，可我早就忘了他上周还帮我复习期末考——看来那句莎士比亚的名言“恶行刻在铜器上，美德写在流水里”真的一点不假。
englishDefinition: This Shakespearian saying expresses the notion that, while we recall well anything done to harm us, we forget quickly the good others do.
example: People often hold onto old grudges far longer than they appreciate kindnesses shown to them, proving that men's evil manners live in brass, while their virtues are written in water.
exampleTranslation: 人们往往对旧怨耿耿于怀，却远不如对他人的善意那样懂得感恩，这正应了那句老话：人的恶行刻在铜器上，而美德却写在流水里。
origin: 出自莎士比亚，喻指人易记他人恶行，却很快淡忘其善行。
note: 莎士比亚名言，书面正式，中性偏感慨，用于感慨人易记怨忘恩，不用于日常口语。 场景考察：情景：你在大学小组项目中，搭档不仅全程划水拖慢进度，还在汇报时抢了你的功劳，可当他后来主动帮你整理复习资料时，你转头就忘了他之前的好意。 例句：I can't stop resenting my old group partner for taking credit for my work, but I already forgot he helped me review for finals last week—guess that Shakespeare quote about evil manners living in brass and virtues written in water is totally true.

definitionCn: “Ménage à trois”是法语，指三人家庭，在英语中它指的是三个人共同生活并彼此发生性关系的一种安排。
englishDefinition: Ménage à trois is French for a household of three, and in English it means an arrangement in which three people live together and have sexual relationships with each other.
example: The 1970s French film explored the complicated emotions and power dynamics of a ménage à trois among three close friends.
exampleTranslation: 这部20世纪70年代的法国电影探讨了三位密友之间一段三角恋关系中复杂的情感与权力博弈。
origin: 源自法语，原指三人同住的家庭，英语中引申为三人两两发生性关系的同居安排。
note: 法语外来俚语，口语非正式，指三人同居并互有性关系，带戏谑或贬义，仅用于熟人私下调侃，正式场合禁用。 场景考察：情景：A curious college student is discussing the origins of common loanwords in English with his language professor during office hours, asking about the meaning of a term he saw referenced in a classic novel. 例句：When the literature student asked her professor about the unusual phrase she encountered in the 18th century novel, she learned that "ménage à trois" refers to a domestic arrangement where three people share a home and maintain mutual romantic and sexual relationships with one another. 翻译：当这名文学系学生向她的教授询问自己在那本18世纪小说里看到的这个特殊短语时，她了解到“ménage à trois”指的是三人共同居住、彼此间保持浪漫与性关系的家庭安排。

definitionCn: 与曾有过分歧的人重建良好关系。
englishDefinition: Re-establish good relations with people one has disagreed with.
example: After their public disagreement, the two politicians decided to meet to mend fences before the upcoming election.
exampleTranslation: 在公开产生分歧后，这两位政治家决定在即将到来的选举前会面，重修旧好。
origin: 源自美国政治，指选举后修复与对手关系，现泛指重修旧好。
note: “Mend fences”为中性口语俚语，适用于修复分歧后的关系，无褒贬，可用于个人或职场人际修复，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你和最好的朋友因为一场关于毕业旅行目的地的激烈争吵已经冷战两周了，你意识到自己当时说话太冲，决定主动约他出来喝杯奶茶，好好聊聊解开误会。 例句：After two weeks of not talking to each other, she decided to mend fences with her best friend by apologizing for her harsh words during their argument. 翻译：在两周互不说话之后，她决定为自己争吵时说的重话道歉，和最好的朋友重归于好。

definitionCn: 圣诞节的传统问候语——常用于圣诞贺卡。
englishDefinition: The traditional greeting at Christmas - very commonly used on Christmas cards.
example: Wishing you a warm and cozy holiday season — Merry Christmas!
exampleTranslation: 祝你度过一个温暖惬意的节日——圣诞快乐！
origin: 源自基督教圣诞传统问候，用于贺卡互致祝福，流传极广。
note: 适用于圣诞节当天口头问候或圣诞贺卡书写，属正式礼貌的通用祝福，无褒贬，可对所有对象使用。 场景考察：情景：圣诞节当天，你在社区超市采购节日食材，遇到了常来买东西的邻居，对方笑着和你打招呼。 例句："Merry Christmas!" I said to my neighbor as we bumped into each other at the grocery store on Christmas morning. 翻译：圣诞节早上，我在杂货店偶遇邻居，对他说道：“圣诞快乐！”

definitionCn: 用于决定飞镖比赛谁先开局的押韵口诀。
englishDefinition: A rhyme used to decide who starts a darts match.
example: We flipped a coin and called "middle for diddle" to see who would throw first in the darts match.
exampleTranslation: 我们抛硬币并喊出“middle for diddle”来决定谁先在飞镖比赛中投掷。
origin: 飞镖比赛选首发的押韵俚语，掷骰定先后时随口念诵，无明确文献出处。
note: 飞镖比赛开场决定先后手的口语押韵用语，非正式场合使用，中性无褒贬，仅适用于参赛选手间，礼貌得体。 场景考察：情景：一群好友在酒吧准备玩飞镖比赛，正纠结谁先开局，有人提议用掷硬币的方式决定先后。 例句：We flipped a coin to decide who would throw first, using the classic "middle for diddle" to settle the start of our darts match. 翻译：我们抛硬币决定谁先投掷，用经典的“猜正反面”来确定飞镖比赛的开局顺序。

definitionCn: 平淡无奇或不得罪人的；选择不偏不倚的。
englishDefinition: Something unadventurous or inoffensive; opting to go neither one way or the other.
example: The band's latest album is solid but a bit middle of the road, lacking the bold experimentation that made their earlier work stand out.
exampleTranslation: 这支乐队的新专辑质量尚可，但有些中规中矩，缺少了让他们早期作品脱颖而出的大胆尝试。
origin: 源自道路中间车道，喻指不偏不倚、无冒险性的中间立场。
note: 口语俚语，中性偏平淡，指平庸无特色、不偏不倚的人或事物，不适合正式场合，无褒贬。 场景考察：情景：班级组织周末短途出游，同学们激烈讨论是去郊外徒步探险，还是去安静的咖啡馆看书放松，班长不想得罪任何一方，提出了一个两边都不偏向的折中方案。 例句：When the class couldn't decide between hiking in the mountains or visiting a quiet bookstore, our monitor suggested a middle-of-the-road plan of walking around the city park. 翻译：当全班同学无法在去山里徒步和逛安静书店之间做出决定时，我们的班长提出了一个走城市公园的折中方案。

definitionCn: “With might and main”的意思是“竭尽全力”。
englishDefinition: With might and main is 'with all of one's strength'.
example: When the building caught fire, the neighbors worked with might and main to break down the door and pull the trapped elderly man to safety.
exampleTranslation: 大楼着火时，邻居们拼尽全力撞开房门，把被困的老人拉到了安全地带。
origin: 古英语短语，源自“mægen”，指倾尽全力、全力以赴。
note: 偏书面正式表达，无褒贬，礼貌中性，用于强调竭尽全力，日常口语少用，不针对特定对象。 场景考察：情景：小明在暴雨来临前，拼尽全力把晾在阳台的被子往屋里拽，生怕被子被雨淋湿。 例句：He pulled the quilt back into the room with might and main before the heavy rain came. 翻译：下大雨前，他拼尽全力把被子拽回了屋里。

word: Mighty oaks from little acorns grow
definitionCn: 伟大的成就往往始于微小的开端。
englishDefinition: Great things may come from small beginnings.
example: When she started her small online handmade jewelry shop in her bedroom, no one expected it to become a global brand, but as the saying goes, mighty oaks from little acorns grow.
exampleTranslation: 当她在自己的卧室里开了那家小小的手工珠宝网店时，没人料到它会成为一个全球品牌，正如俗语所说，万丈高楼平地起。
origin: 源自英语谚语，喻指参天橡树由小橡果长成，伟大事业始于微小开端。
note: 口语化励志谚语，褒义，适用于鼓励他人从小处起步，正式场合少用，无冒犯性。 场景考察：情景：你刚加入学校的编程社团，只会写简单的代码片段，看着学长学姐们开发出能帮全校同学查询课表的实用小程序，觉得自己离做出有用的成果还很远。 例句：When you first learn to code, it's hard to imagine building useful apps one day, but mighty oaks from little acorns grow. 翻译：当你刚开始学编程时，很难想象自己有一天能开发出实用的应用程序，但万丈高楼平地起，伟大的成就往往始于微小的起步。

definitionCn: 关心和同情他人。
englishDefinition: Care and compassion for others.
example: Even after being unfairly blamed for the project failure, she showed her milk of human kindness by helping her former team revise their proposal for the next quarter.
exampleTranslation: 即便在被不公平地指责为项目失败的责任人后，她仍心怀恻隐之心，主动帮助之前的团队修改下一季度的项目提案。
origin: 源自莎士比亚《麦克白》，麦克白夫人指责丈夫天生缺乏对他人的善意与怜悯。
note: 正式书面语，褒义，指对他人的善意与同情，适用于文学、评论等正式语境，不宜日常口语使用。 场景考察：情景：A student accidentally knocks over a classmate's full lunch tray in the crowded school cafeteria, spilling soup all over their uniform. 例句：Even though she was in a rush to catch the bus, the stranger showed her milk of human kindness by helping her pick up all the scattered groceries and walking her home. 翻译：尽管她急着赶公交，那位陌生人还是出于恻隐之心帮她捡起所有散落的杂货，并陪她走回了家。

definitionCn: 翻译成中文"""Mince pies is Cockney rhyming slang for eyes."""
englishDefinition: Mince pies is Cockney rhyming slang for eyes.
example: When he heard the news, his mince pies went wide with shock.
exampleTranslation: 他听到这个消息时，惊讶得瞪大了双眼。
origin: 源自伦敦考克尼押韵俚语，以“mince pies”与“eyes”押韵代指眼睛。
note: 伦敦东区俚语，表眼睛，口语非正式，礼貌中性，仅熟人间用，正式场合禁用。 场景考察：情景：在伦敦东区的酒吧里，一位老调酒师正和朋友聊起刚走进来的年轻女孩，他想提醒朋友注意女孩明亮的眼睛。 例句："Did you see those mince pies on that girl?" remarked the barman to his friend. 翻译：“你看到那个女孩的眼睛了吗？”调酒师对他的朋友说道。

definitionCn: 委婉咒骂语是委婉语的一个子类别，用于在表达惊讶或恼怒时避免说脏话。
englishDefinition: Minced oaths are a sub-group of euphemisms used to avoid swearing when expressing surprise or annoyance.
example: When she accidentally spilled coffee all over her laptop, she muttered "fudge sticks" under her breath, a classic minced oath that conveyed her frustration without breaking her no-swearing rule.
exampleTranslation: 当她不小心把咖啡洒了一整台笔记本电脑时，她低声嘟囔了一句“fudge sticks”，这是一句典型的委婉咒骂，既表达了她的懊恼，又没有违反她不骂人的规矩。
origin: 源自英语委婉语，为避免冒犯，将粗话替换为谐音或近义的温和表达。
note: 口语非正式，用于表达惊讶或烦躁时替代粗口，语气委婉礼貌，无褒贬，适用于日常熟人交流，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你正准备享用刚做好的、淋满奶油的热咖啡，突然被路过的人撞了一下，咖啡全洒在了新买的白衬衫上，你下意识脱口而出一句委婉的咒骂。 例句："Oh fudge!" she exclaimed when she saw the coffee spill all over her new white shirt. 翻译：“哦，真倒霉！”看到咖啡洒了自己的新白衬衫，她惊呼道。

definitionCn: 被形容为“头脑像捕兽夹一样”的人，能以异乎寻常的速度和敏锐度理解、记忆事物，或是对事物做出反应。
englishDefinition: Someone described as having a mind like a steel trap grasps, remembers, or reacts to things with unusual speed and sharpness.
example: Even at 82, my grandma has a mind like a steel trap—she can recall the exact details of events that happened 60 years ago without missing a single word.
exampleTranslation: 即使已经82岁了，我奶奶的脑子还是像捕兽夹一样敏锐——她能一字不差地回忆起60年前发生的事情的具体细节。
origin: 源自19世纪美国，喻思维如钢制捕兽夹般敏捷锐利，反应迅速、记忆牢固。
note: 口语褒义俚语，非正式场合使用，礼貌无冒犯，用于夸赞他人思维敏捷、记性好，不适合正式文书。 场景考察：情景：A college student who just started learning a new programming language amazes their classmates by recalling every syntax rule, function parameter, and debugging tip the instructor mentioned in the first lecture, even when the instructor randomly quizzes them a week later. 例句：My roommate is only 19, but she has a mind like a steel trap—she can remember every detail of the textbook chapters she read just once last semester and explain complex formulas to me without even glancing at her notes. 翻译：我的室友才19岁，但她的脑子转得快极了——她能记住上学期只看过一遍的课本章节里的所有细节，甚至不用看笔记就能给我讲解复杂的公式。

definitionCn: 指责他人停止说脏话或说话更礼貌的话语。
englishDefinition: A reproach telling someone to stop swearing or to speak more politely.
example: If you keep using such foul words in front of the kids, I'll have to tell you to mind your language.
exampleTranslation: 如果你继续在孩子们面前说这种脏话，我就得提醒你注意言辞了。
origin: 源自日常英语劝诫，提醒他人注意言辞，勿说脏话或保持礼貌。
note: 口语化责备语，礼貌程度低，带负面情绪，用于提醒他人停止说脏话或注意言辞，不适合正式场合。 场景考察：情景：在安静的图书馆里，你的同学因为找不到想看的书，忍不住大声说了句脏话，周围的读者都皱起了眉头看向他。例句：Mind your language! This is a quiet reading area, please don't swear. 翻译：注意你的言辞！这里是安静的阅览区，请不要说脏话。

definitionCn: 表现得体；注意言辞。
englishDefinition: Be on your best behaviour; be careful of your language.
example: When you attend the formal dinner with the CEO, make sure to mind your Ps and Qs—no casual jokes or slang.
exampleTranslation: 当你和首席执行官一起参加正式晚宴时，一定要注意言行举止得体——不要说随意的笑话或俚语。
origin: 源自英国酒馆，提醒顾客留意酒账，后引申为谨言慎行。
note: 口语化提醒，无褒贬，礼貌中性，用于提醒他人注意言行举止，不适用正式文书。 场景考察：情景：你即将去拜访一位非常讲究礼仪的外国教授，教授平时对学生的言行举止要求很高，你需要提醒自己在教授家做客时注意言行得体。 例句：When you visit your professor's house this weekend, mind your Ps and Qs and don't make any rude comments. 翻译：这周末你去教授家做客的时候，要注意言行得体，不要说任何无礼的话。

definitionCn: 一个人的听觉记忆或想象。
englishDefinition: One's aural memory or imagination.
example: When I read the poem aloud, my mind's ear could almost hear the poet's original voice reciting it with that familiar, gentle lilt.
exampleTranslation: 当我大声朗读这首诗时，我的心耳几乎能听见诗人原本用那熟悉温柔的语调吟诵它的声音。
origin: 源自莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》，指人脑中的听觉想象与记忆，即“心耳”。
note: 用于口语或文学语境，指脑中的听觉记忆或想象，中性文雅，无褒贬，不适合正式公文。 场景考察：情景：一位退休多年的老钢琴家坐在安静的客厅里，指尖轻轻摩挲着旧琴键，脑海中清晰浮现出多年前演奏过的经典旋律。 例句：The retired pianist could hear the entire sonata in her mind's ear, even though the piano in front of her was silent. 翻译：这位退休的钢琴家即使面前的钢琴毫无声响，也能在脑海的听觉想象中听见整首奏鸣曲。

definitionCn: 完美或崭新的状态，令人联想到刚铸造出来的硬币。
englishDefinition: A condition of perfection or newness suggestive of that of a freshly minted coin.
example: My grandfather still keeps his 1965 Mustang in mint condition, with not a single scratch on the glossy paint.
exampleTranslation: 我祖父把他1965年款的野马汽车保存得完好如新，光亮的车漆上连一道划痕都没有。
origin: 源自铸币厂新铸硬币的完美状态，喻指物品崭新完好、毫无瑕疵。
note: 口语化褒义俚语，用于描述物品完好如新，礼貌得体，可对各类对象使用，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你在二手书店淘到了一本1990年出版的绝版老漫画，翻开后发现书页没有折痕、没有涂鸦，连书角都完全平整，和刚从印刷厂出来的状态一模一样。 例句：Even though this comic book is 30 years old, it is in mint condition with no dog-ears or markings at all. 翻译：尽管这本漫画书已经有30年历史了，它却完好如新，连一点折痕或标记都没有。

word: Misery acquaints a man with strange bedfellows
phonetic: /ˈmɪzəri əˈkweɪnts ə mæn wɪð streɪndʒ ˈbɛdˌfɛləʊz/
definitionCn: 倾盆大雨里错过末班车后，我不得不和三个陌生人挤在一辆狭小的出租车上赶回市区——患难之中，人总会和素不相识的人结伴。
englishDefinition: From Shakespeare's The Tempest, 1610: Alas, the storm is come again! my best way is to creep under his gaberdine; there is no other shelter hereabouts: misery acquaints a man with strange bed-fellows. I will here shroud till the dregs of the storm be past.
example: After getting stranded together in the mountain cabin during the blizzard, the two strangers realized that misery acquaints a man with strange bedfellows, as they shared blankets and told stories to pass the time.
exampleTranslation: 暴风雪中被困在山间小屋里后，这两个陌生人意识到“患难使人结识奇怪的同床伙伴”——他们共用毯子、讲故事打发时间。
origin: 出自莎士比亚1610年《暴风雨》，指困境中人会与原本不相干的人共处。
note: 源自莎翁《暴风雨》，偏书面，中性无褒贬，指困境中结识意外同伴，不用于日常口语。 场景考察：情景：你在陌生城市赶早班火车时睡过了头，一路狂奔到车站却发现列车因暴雪全面停运，你又冷又饿，手机也没电关机，只能和同样滞留的陌生旅客挤在车站狭小的临时候车棚里，盖着别人递来的陌生毛毯凑合一晚。 例句：After missing the last bus home in the pouring rain, I had to share a cramped taxi with three strangers to get back to the city — misery acquaints a man with strange bedfellows.

definitionCn: 习惯性发牢骚的人。
englishDefinition: A habitual grumbler.
example: Don't be such a Moaning Minnie — the rain will clear up soon, and we can still go for our picnic.
exampleTranslation: 别老是唉声叹气地抱怨了——雨很快就会停，我们还是可以去野餐的。
origin: 源自二战英军对爱抱怨士兵的戏称，后泛指习惯性发牢骚的人。
note: 口语俚语，带贬义，指习惯性抱怨的人，非正式场合使用，对他人使用不礼貌。 场景考察：情景：在大学宿舍里，室友们正一起准备周末的短途徒步旅行，大家都在兴奋地讨论路线和要带的零食，只有Tom一直在抱怨天气可能会下雨、背包太重、鞋子磨脚，完全扫了大家的兴。 例句：We were all getting excited about the picnic, but Dave was being such a Moaning Minnie, complaining that it was too hot, the food was boring, and the flies were annoying. 翻译：我们都对这次野餐感到很兴奋，戴夫却一直在唉声叹气地抱怨，说天气太热、食物没意思、苍蝇也烦人。

definitionCn: 几乎不费力气就能获得丰厚回报。
englishDefinition: A profitable return for little effort.
example: Working as a part-time campus tutor is money for old rope for him, since he already has a solid grasp of the subject and only needs to spend a few hours a week helping students with their assignments.
exampleTranslation: 对他来说，做兼职校园辅导员简直是不费吹灰之力就能赚钱的美差，因为他本来就对这门学科了如指掌，每周只需要花几个小时帮学生辅导作业就行。
origin: 源自旧时卖旧绳获利，喻轻松付出却能获得丰厚回报。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，中性偏褒，指轻松获利，勿用于正式文书或严肃商务沟通。 场景考察：情景：你在社区公告栏看到一则兼职广告，对方以时薪25美元的报酬，聘请你帮忙整理自家车库里的旧工具和杂物，这份工作几乎不需要耗费什么体力，报酬却相当丰厚。 例句：Getting paid $25 an hour to sort out old tools in someone's garage was money for old rope. 翻译：每小时赚25美元去帮人整理车库里的旧工具，这活儿真是轻松又赚钱。

definitionCn: 一种带有贬义的描述，常被反对者用来形容女权主义者或行为粗野的女性。
englishDefinition: A disparaging description, often used to describe feminist or rowdy women by their detractors.
example: The old conservative politician dismissed the new wave of female candidates as just another monstrous regiment of women, completely ignoring their well-researched policy proposals.
exampleTranslation: 那位老派的保守派政客将这股女性候选人的新潮流斥为不过是又一群“可怕的女性军团”，完全无视了她们经过充分调研的政策提案。
origin: 源自17世纪苏格兰宗教改革家约翰·诺克斯抨击女性统治的著作，后被引申为贬损女权或喧闹女性的说法。
note: 口语贬义，用于贬损女权或喧闹女性，正式场合禁用，对女性使用易冒犯。 场景考察：情景：A conservative local newspaper columnist writes a scathing opinion piece criticizing a group of women who organized a large, unpermitted protest demanding equal pay for female workers, framing their advocacy as overly aggressive and unwelcome. 例句：The columnist dismissed the grassroots equal pay protest led by local working women as nothing more than a monstrous regiment of women, refusing to engage with their core demands for fair compensation. 翻译：这位专栏作家将当地职业女性发起的草根同工同酬抗议斥为不过是“凶悍女性的暴政”，拒绝回应她们提出的公平薪酬核心诉求。

definitionCn: 腹泻（在美国拼写为 diarrhea），即游客前往外国地区旅行时常会遭遇的腹泻。
englishDefinition: The diarrhoea (spelled in America as diarrhea) that is often suffered by tourists when travelling to foreign parts.
example: After eating street food from the unhygienic stall during her trip to Mexico, she was struck down by Montezuma's revenge and had to stay in her hotel room for two days.
exampleTranslation: 在墨西哥旅行时，她吃了卫生条件不达标的路边摊食物后，不幸患上了旅行者腹泻，不得不卧床在酒店房间里待了两天。
origin: 源自阿兹特克皇帝蒙特祖马二世，喻指游客赴外旅行常患的腹泻。
note: 口语俚语，带戏谑调侃色彩，非正式场合使用，礼貌度低，仅用于熟人闲聊，勿对腹泻患者当面提及。 场景考察：情景：你和刚从东南亚背包旅行回来的朋友聊天，对方一脸疲惫地说自己刚结束为期两周的泰国行程，却在返程前一天因为吃了路边摊的青木瓜沙拉，突然开始频繁跑厕所，连赶飞机的力气都快没了。 例句：My friend spent the last day of her Thailand trip bedridden with Montezuma's revenge after trying a spicy street-food salad. 翻译：我朋友在泰国尝试了一份辣味街头沙拉后，最后一天因旅行者腹泻卧床不起。

definitionCn: 一个不相关的论点。
englishDefinition: An irrelevant argument.
example: Whether we take the bus or the subway to the exhibition is a moot point, since both routes take roughly the same amount of time.
exampleTranslation: 我们坐公交还是地铁去看展览是个没有意义的问题，因为两条路线耗时差不多。
origin: 源自古英语“moot”，原指议事会讨论的议题，现指无实际意义、无关紧要的争论。
note: 口语非正式场合使用，无褒贬，指无实际意义的争论，避免用于正式文书或严肃讨论。 场景考察：情景：两个朋友为了“已经过期的电影票能不能退”争论了半小时，后来才想起这张票根本不是他们买的。 例句：Since the ticket isn't ours, whether we can get a refund is a moot point. 翻译：既然这张票不是我们的，能不能退票根本就是个无意义的争论。

definitionCn: 体重过高，足以对健康构成严重风险的状态。
englishDefinition: The condition of having a body weight high enough to pose a severe risk to health.
example: Doctors warned that his morbid obesity would likely lead to life-threatening complications if he did not undergo immediate medical intervention.
exampleTranslation: 医生警告称，如果他不立即接受医疗干预，他的病态肥胖很可能会引发危及生命的并发症。
origin: 源自医学术语，指体重过高已严重威胁健康的病态肥胖状态。
note: 医学术语，正式书面语，无褒贬，用于临床诊断或健康科普，描述体重过高危及健康的病理状态。 场景考察：情景：社区医院的健康宣教课上，医生正在向居民讲解不同程度肥胖对健康的影响，提到了体重过高到足以严重威胁健康的状态。 例句：Morbid obesity is a serious medical condition that requires professional medical intervention to manage safely. 翻译：病态肥胖是一种严重的疾病，需要专业的医疗干预才能安全地进行管理。

definitionCn: 物超所值。
englishDefinition: More for your money.
example: Switching to this affordable wireless earbud model gives you more bang for your buck, with crisp sound quality and 24-hour battery life at half the price of premium brands.
exampleTranslation: 换用这款平价无线耳机性价比超高，音质清晰、续航长达24小时，价格却只有高端品牌的一半。
origin: 源自美国，指以同等花费获得更多收益，性价比更高。
note: 口语化表达，褒义，用于夸赞商品性价比高，非正式场合，对商家或服务方使用，无冒犯性。 场景考察：情景：你在超市选购洗衣液，发现同品牌的常规款售价50元、容量2升，而促销装售价60元、容量3升，单位容量的价格更低，性价比更高。 例句：This 3-liter laundry detergent is more bang for your buck compared to the 2-liter regular one. 翻译：和2升的常规款相比，这款3升的洗衣液性价比更高。

definitionCn: 用于回应那些声称自己做了某件明显愚蠢之事的人。
englishDefinition: Said in reply to someone who has reported doing something that is considered to be obviously foolish.
example: You actually paid double the asking price for that old phone? More fool you!
exampleTranslation: 你居然为那台旧手机付了双倍的要价？你可真傻！
origin: 英式口语，用于回应他人做了明显蠢事，意为“你可真傻”。
note: 口语非正式表达，带调侃惋惜意味，用于熟人，不适合正式场合，勿对陌生人使用。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友为了抢限量款球鞋，在零下的冬夜排了整整六个小时的队，结果到店才发现这款球鞋根本没有他的尺码，他还冻得重感冒了，你对着他说出这句俚语。 例句：You queued for six hours in the freezing cold just to find out they didn't have your size? More fool you! 翻译：你在大冷天排了六个小时的队，结果才发现没有你的尺码？你可真是太傻了！

definitionCn: 这句谚语表明，如果你试图仓促行事，就会犯错，最终反而耗费更多时间。
englishDefinition: This proverbial saying suggest that, if you try and do something quickly you will make mistakes and take longer in the end.
example: Don't rush through your exam paper just to finish early—you'll likely make careless errors and have to redo parts of it; remember, more haste, less speed.
exampleTranslation: 别为了提前交卷就匆匆忙忙答题，你很可能会犯粗心的错误，还得回头重做部分题目，记住，欲速则不达。
origin: 源自英语谚语，指急于求成反易出错，最终耗时更长，欲速则不达。
note: 多用于口语或非正式写作，中性劝诫，无褒贬，适用于急于求成的人，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：You have a 10-page history essay due tomorrow, but you rush through it without checking facts or organizing your ideas, so you end up with messy paragraphs and have to rewrite half of it. 例句：You forgot to double-check your essay and had to rewrite half of it—more haste, less speed. 翻译：你忘了检查论文，最后不得不重写一半——欲速则不达。

word: More honoured in the breach than in the observance
phonetic: /mɔː ˈhɒnəd ɪn ðə briːtʃ ðæn ɪn ði əbˈzɜːvəns/
definitionCn: 这通常被认为是指一条被违反的次数多于被遵守的次数的规则。但该剧的上下文表明，其真正含义是“违背它比遵守它更光荣”。
englishDefinition: This is usually thought to mean a rule which is more often broken than observed. The context of the play shows the real meaning as 'it is more honourable to breach than to observe'.
example: Many outdated workplace policies are more honoured in the breach than in the observance, with even long-time employees rarely following them strictly.
exampleTranslation: 许多过时的职场规定实际上是遵守的人少、违反的人多，就连老员工也很少严格遵守。
origin: 源自莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》，原义为违反比遵守更体面，现多被误解为规则常遭违反。
note: 该俚语偏书面正式，多用于批评规则形同虚设，语气中性偏讽刺，适用于正式评论或文学语境，不宜用于日常口语。 场景考察：情景：学校规定学生在校期间必须穿全套校服，但实际上绝大多数学生都只穿校服外套，内搭自己的休闲T恤，连老师也对这种普遍情况睁一只眼闭一只眼。 例句：The school's rule requiring full uniform is more honoured in the breach than in the observance. 翻译：这所学校要求穿全套校服的规定，更多时候是被违反而非被遵守。

definitionCn: 与一天中的晚些时候相比，早上状态更好的人。
englishDefinition: Someone who functions better in the morning, as compared to later in the day.
example: As a morning person, I always finish my most demanding work tasks before 10 a.m., when my focus and energy are at their peak.
exampleTranslation: 作为一个习惯早起的人，我总是在上午10点前完成最费神的工作任务，因为那时候我的专注力和精力都处于巅峰状态。
origin: 源自日常作息描述，指早晨精力充沛、状态更佳的人，与夜猫子相对。
note: 口语化表达，无褒贬，礼貌中性，用于日常闲聊，描述习惯早起、上午状态更佳的人。 场景考察：情景：你身边有位朋友每天早上六点就起床，精神饱满地晨跑、做早餐、处理工作，到了晚上九点就困得睁不开眼，而你自己早上总是起不来，要到下午才进入状态。 例句：My roommate is such a morning person that she finishes all her work before noon, while I can barely open my eyes in the early morning. 翻译：我的室友是个特别习惯早起的人，她中午之前就能把所有工作做完，而我早上连眼睛都睁不开。

definitionCn: 一个人的故土，或其祖先的故土。
englishDefinition: One's native land, or the native land of one's ancestors.
example: For many overseas Chinese, their mother country is a source of deep pride and nostalgia, no matter how far they wander.
exampleTranslation: 对许多海外华人来说，无论漂泊多远，祖国都是他们深深的自豪与乡愁之源。
origin: 源自殖民时期，指移民母国，现泛指本人或祖先的故土。
note: “Mother country”偏书面，正式场合可用，带褒义，指祖国或祖籍国，对长辈、正式交流对象使用均得体。 场景考察：情景：海外华人在海外生活多年，每逢传统节日都会和家人一起翻看老照片，聊起祖辈从国内迁居海外的往事，这时可以用这个俚语表达对故土的眷恋。 例句：Every time she talks about her mother country, she can't help but think of the small courtyard where she spent her childhood. 翻译：每次聊起自己的祖国，她都忍不住想起自己童年生活过的那个小院。

definitionCn: 一群形形色色、看不出有什么共同点，而且往往难以管束的人。
englishDefinition: A group of people of many different types who do not obviously belong together, and often an unruly one.
example: The newly formed expedition team was a motley crew, with members ranging from seasoned mountain climbers to amateur photographers who had never set foot in the wilderness.
exampleTranslation: 这支新组建的探险队是个鱼龙混杂的队伍，成员既有经验丰富的登山者，也有从未踏足过荒野的业余摄影师。
origin: 源自莎士比亚《亨利四世》，指身份混杂、不守规矩的一群人。
note: 口语非正式，略带贬义，指混杂难管的群体，勿用于正式场合或描述他人团队。 场景考察：情景：你刚加入学校的户外探险社团，第一次参加周末徒步活动时，发现社团成员里有擅长攀岩的体育生、热爱拍风景的摄影爱好者、会辨认野生植物的生物系学生，还有专门负责给大家准备零食的吃货同学，这群背景完全不同的人凑在一起热热闹闹出发的场景。 例句：Our hiking club is a motley crew, but we always have the best adventures together. 翻译：我们的徒步社团是个由各色人等组成的团体，但我们在一起总能拥有最棒的冒险经历。

definitionCn: 美味；好吃到让你流口水。
englishDefinition: Delicious; tasty enough to make you salivate.
example: The aroma of freshly baked cinnamon rolls drifting from the kitchen was absolutely mouth-watering.
exampleTranslation: 厨房里飘来的刚出炉的肉桂卷香气实在令人垂涎欲滴。
origin: 源自食物香气刺激唾液分泌的生理反应，形容食物美味诱人，令人垂涎。
note: 口语化褒义表达，用于形容食物诱人，礼貌得体，可对亲友、服务人员使用，正式场合宜用delicious。 场景考察：情景：周末你路过街角新开的面包店，玻璃柜里刚出炉的黄油牛角包表皮金黄酥脆，还飘着暖烘烘的甜香，你站在店门口忍不住咽了下口水。 例句：The smell of freshly baked croissants from the corner bakery was absolutely mouth-watering. 翻译：街角面包店刚出炉的牛角包香气简直让人垂涎欲滴。

definitionCn: 将某种情形或环境改变到可被注意、可被识别且可被测量的程度。
englishDefinition: To change a situation or circumstance to a noticeable, or discernible, and measurable amount.
example: Even a small adjustment to the marketing strategy can move the needle on brand awareness among young consumers.
exampleTranslation: 哪怕对营销策略做一点小调整，也能显著提升年轻消费者群体的品牌认知度。
origin: 源自医疗测针，指针移动代表读数变化，喻指产生可衡量的显著改变。
note: 商务职场口语，中性偏褒，用于工作汇报、项目讨论，不适合正式文书或日常闲聊。 场景考察：情景：一家创业公司的产品团队连续三个月优化用户留存功能，却始终没有看到核心数据的明显变化，团队负责人在周会上鼓励大家不要放弃，要找到能真正推动数据增长的突破口。 例句：The product team tried every small tweak to the onboarding flow, but none of them moved the needle on user retention until they added the one-click import feature. 翻译：产品团队对新手引导流程做了各种小调整，但都没能让用户留存率出现明显变化，直到他们加入了一键导入功能。

definitionCn: 精神饱满、能主动发起变革并影响事态发展的人。
englishDefinition: People of energetic demeanour, who initiate change and influence events.
example: As one of the most prominent movers and shakers in the tech industry, she has spearheaded multiple groundbreaking initiatives that have reshaped how people interact with digital products.
exampleTranslation: 作为科技行业最具影响力的推动者之一，她牵头开展了多项开创性项目，重塑了人们与数字产品互动的方式。
origin: 源自19世纪英国诗人奥肖内西诗作，指积极推动变革、有影响力的实干者。
note: 口语褒义俚语，用于形容精力充沛、能推动变革、影响事态的核心人物，不适合正式文书，对同辈或公众人物使用均可。 场景考察：情景：学校举办年度学生领导力峰会，邀请了本地几位在社区公益、青年创业领域做出突出成绩的年轻校友返校分享，他们都是敢想敢干、能带动身边人一起推动项目落地的核心人物。 例句：The movers and shakers behind the city's new youth volunteer program gathered at the town hall to discuss next year's expansion plans. 翻译：推动本市全新青年志愿项目落地的几位核心实干人物齐聚市政厅，共同商讨明年的项目拓展计划。

definitionCn: 单方面改变进程或竞争的目标，以获取优势。
englishDefinition: Changing the target of a process or competition to by one side in order to gain advantage.
example: Whenever we got close to finishing the project on time, our manager kept moving the goalposts by adding new requirements.
exampleTranslation: 每当我们快要按时完成项目时，经理就会不断提出新要求，临时改变目标。
origin: 源自体育赛事，指擅自移动球门柱，比喻为获利单方面改变规则。
note: 口语俚语，非正式，带贬义，指擅自改规则谋利，多用于批评他人，不宜正式场合或礼貌表述。 场景考察：情景：小明报名参加了学校的数学竞赛，原本的比赛规则是只要在初赛中答对80%的题目就能晋级决赛，他认真复习后顺利达到了这个标准，结果组委会临时修改规则，要求答对90%才能晋级，这就是典型的“Moving the goalposts”行为。 例句：The competition organizers moved the goalposts by raising the passing score from 80% to 90% right after the preliminary round. 翻译：竞赛组委会在初赛后临时把及格线从80%提高到90%，这是在故意改变规则占便宜。

definitionCn: “无事生非”的意思是“对一件无关紧要的事情大惊小怪”。
englishDefinition: 'Much ado about nothing' means 'a great deal of fuss over a thing of little importance'.
example: Don't get so upset about a minor typo in the email—this is just much ado about nothing.
exampleTranslation: 别为邮件里一个小小的拼写错误这么生气——这完全是无事生非。
origin: 源自莎士比亚同名喜剧，指为无关紧要的事大动干戈、小题大做。
note: 口语化表达，中性偏调侃，非正式场合用，指小题大做，勿用于严肃正式语境。 场景考察：情景：周末你兴冲冲地准备了一大桌零食、布置好投影，约好朋友来家里看期待已久的新电影，结果朋友临时爽约，你忙活半天的准备最后全白费了。 例句：All the snacks and decorations I prepared for the movie night turned out to be much ado about nothing when my friend canceled at the last minute. 翻译：我为电影之夜准备的所有零食和装饰，在朋友最后一刻取消时都成了小题大做、白费功夫。

definitionCn: 相似——难以区分。
englishDefinition: Similar - difficult to distinguish.
example: After tasting both premium coffee brands side by side, I found they were much of a muchness, with no noticeable difference in aroma or flavor.
exampleTranslation: 在并排品尝了这两个高端咖啡品牌后，我发现它们大同小异，在香气和口味上没有明显区别。
origin: 源自18世纪，原指事物差异极小，现形容两者相似难辨。
note: 口语非正式表达，礼貌中性，无褒贬，用于日常闲聊，形容事物差别极小、难以区分，不适合正式文书或严肃场合。 场景考察：情景：你在咖啡店纠结选两款看起来几乎一模一样的手工曲奇，店员告诉你它们的口味差别很小，你可以随意挑选。 例句：When comparing the two homemade cookies, they taste much of a muchness, so you can pick either one. 翻译：对比这两款手工曲奇的时候，它们的味道几乎没什么差别，所以你随便选哪一款都行。

definitionCn: “反复琢磨某事”指的是以反思的方式在脑海中反复思考这件事。
englishDefinition: To 'mull something over' is to turn it over in one's mind, in a reflective way.
example: I need a few days to mull over your job offer before giving you a final answer.
exampleTranslation: 我需要几天时间仔细考虑你的工作邀请，再给你最终答复。
origin: 源自酿酒时麦芽反复浸渍搅拌，喻指反复思索、仔细考量某事。
note: 口语化表达，中性无褒贬，适用于日常思考斟酌场景，正式文书少用，可对人或对己使用。 场景考察：情景：周末你收到了心仪大学的录取通知，但同时也拿到了另一份高薪实习offer，你需要花几天时间权衡哪个选择更符合自己的长期规划。 例句：I need a few days to mull over whether to accept the university offer or take the internship. 翻译：我需要几天时间仔细考虑是接受大学录取通知还是去做那份实习。

definitionCn: “Mum's the word”的意思是“保持安静——什么也别说”。
englishDefinition: 'Mum's the word' means 'keep quiet - say nothing'.
example: I know you're upset about the surprise party, but mum's the word until the big day!
exampleTranslation: 我知道你对这场惊喜派对的事感到郁闷，但在派对当天之前你可千万要守口如瓶啊！
origin: 源自莎士比亚剧作，“mum”拟闭唇发声，喻严守秘密，意为保持沉默、守口如瓶。
note: 口语化表达，表保密，语气中性，适用于熟人或非正式场合，正式文书慎用，对长辈或上级使用需注意分寸。 场景考察：情景：你和好朋友约好，要在妈妈生日当天偷偷给她准备惊喜派对，还买好了她最爱的奶油蛋糕藏在冰箱里，你拉着好朋友的手叮嘱道。 例句：Mum's the word about the surprise party for Mum, okay? 翻译：关于给妈妈准备惊喜派对的事，要保密哦，好吗？

definitionCn: 胡说八道，尤指毫无意义的言语，且常与虚假的宗教仪式相关联。
englishDefinition: Nonsense, especially meaningless speech and often associated with spurious religious ritual.
example: Don't waste time listening to that mumbo jumbo about the new product's magical healing powers; it's just a marketing gimmick.
exampleTranslation: 别浪费时间听那些关于这款新产品有神奇疗效的胡言乱语，那不过是营销噱头罢了。
origin: 源自西非神灵名，后指无意义、晦涩难懂的言语或仪式。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，略带贬义，指无意义的胡言乱语，对熟人吐槽时可用，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你在听一位自称“灵性导师”的人用一堆没人听得懂的神秘术语讲了半小时，朋友悄悄问你他到底在说什么。 例句：I couldn't understand a word of what that self-proclaimed guru was saying; it was all just mumbo jumbo about cosmic vibrations and ancient secrets. 翻译：那位自称大师的人说的话我一个字也听不懂，全是关于宇宙振动和古老秘密的莫名其妙的胡言乱语。

definitionCn: 所谓的定律通常被表述为：“凡是可能出错的事，就一定会出错。”
englishDefinition: The so-called law is usually expressed as 'If anything can go wrong, it will'.
example: I was running late for the meeting, and of course, I missed the bus—classic Murphy's Law.
exampleTranslation: 我开会快迟到了，结果还错过了公交车，这就是典型的墨菲定律。
origin: 源自美国空军墨菲上尉的工程失误轶事，指凡可能出错的事终将出错。
note: 口语非正式场合，中性偏调侃，用于吐槽意外失误，勿在严肃正式场合使用。 场景考察：情景：周末你精心准备了野餐，提前把三明治、水果、饮料都装进背包，还特意查了天气预报说全天晴朗，结果刚到公园铺开野餐垫，突然下起了阵雨，你手忙脚乱收拾东西时，背包里的果汁还不小心洒了出来。 例句：Just as I was about to enjoy my outdoor picnic, it started pouring rain and my juice spilled everywhere—classic Murphy's Law! 翻译：就在我准备好好享受户外野餐的时候，突然下起了瓢泼大雨，我的果汁还洒了一地——典型的墨菲定律啊！

word: Music has charms to soothe the savage breast
phonetic: /ˈmjuːzɪk hæz tʃɑːmz tuː suːð ðə ˈsævɪdʒ brest/
definitionCn: 篮球赛输了之后，我的朋友怒不可遏，拒绝和任何人说话，但放他最喜欢的轻柔钢琴曲起了作用——音乐有抚慰狂暴心灵的力量，十分钟后他就冷静下来了。
englishDefinition: Literal meaning. That literal meaning is open to misinterpretation as this phrase is frequently written as 'music has charms to soothe the savage beast'.
example: Many people mistakenly quote the old saying as "music has charms to soothe the savage beast", but the original line refers to the breast, not an animal.
exampleTranslation: 很多人错误地把那句老话引用为“音乐拥有抚慰野兽的魅力”，但原句指的是人的胸怀，而非某种动物。
origin: 源自康格里夫戏剧，原指抚慰粗野心胸，常被误写为“抚慰野兽”。
note: 该俚语为书面语，褒义，用于强调音乐的治愈力量，正式场合可用，无冒犯性，不适合指代真实的人或兽。 场景考察：情景：你的好朋友刚结束一场激烈的篮球比赛，因为输球情绪非常激动，坐在场边生气地摔水瓶、抱怨队友，你拿出手机放了一首他平时最喜欢的舒缓纯音乐，没过多久他的情绪就慢慢平复下来了。 例句：After losing the basketball game, my friend was furious and refused to talk to anyone, but playing his favorite soft piano music worked—music has charms to soothe the savage breast, and he calmed down in ten minutes.

definitionCn: 当写作并读作Mutt 'n' Jeff时，它的意思是聋的。它也是一个俚语，指警察审讯时的“好警察/坏警察”方法，或指任何其他在大小或性质上形成对比的两个人或物。
englishDefinition: When written and pronounced as Mutt 'n' Jeff this has the meaning deaf. It is also a slang term for the 'good cop/bad cop' method of police interrogation or any other pair of people or items which are contrasting in size or nature.
example: The veteran detective and his rookie partner were often mistaken for a Mutt 'n' Jeff pair, with the towering senior officer towering over his much shorter new recruit.
exampleTranslation: 这位资深侦探和他的菜鸟搭档常被人看作是一对“Mutt 'n' Jeff”式的反差组合——身材高大的老警官比他矮得多的新入职搭档高出一大截。
origin: 源自同名漫画，谐音指耳聋，也指一好一坏的审讯搭档或反差组合。
note: 英式俚语，口语非正式，无褒贬。表“聋”或反差搭档，勿用于正式场合，避免对听障人士冒犯。 场景考察：情景：两名社区志愿者在老年活动中心搭档开展反诈宣传，一位性格热情外放、语速极快，另一位沉稳内敛、说话慢条斯理，两人风格反差极大，居民们都笑着说这对搭档配合得特别好。 例句：The two volunteers running the anti-fraud outreach at the senior center are total Mutt and Jeff: one is super bubbly and talks a mile a minute, while the other is quiet and soft-spoken, but they make a great team. 翻译：在老年活动中心开展反诈宣传的两名志愿者完全是一对反差搭档：一个热情外放、语速飞快，另一个安静沉稳、说话轻声细语，但他们配合得特别好。

definitionCn: “老来俏”是一句贬损之词，针对的是那些打扮得比实际年龄年轻许多的年长女性。
englishDefinition: 'Mutton dressed as lamb' is a put-down aimed at an ageing woman who is dressed or made up of someone much younger.
example: My aunt got a tattoo and started wearing crop tops after she turned fifty, and everyone said she was mutton dressed as lamb.
exampleTranslation: 我姑姑五十岁后纹了身，开始穿露脐装，大家都说她是老黄瓜刷绿漆——装嫩。
origin: 源自英国俚语，指老妇打扮得像少女，以羊肉喻老，羊羔喻少，讽刺装嫩。
note: 口语贬义俚语，用于嘲讽年长女性刻意扮嫩，不礼貌，仅限非正式场合，勿当面使用。 场景考察：情景：A 55-year-old woman shows up at a college party in a crop top, mini skirt, and heavy glittery makeup meant for 20-year-olds, and her friend whispers to you that she’s trying way too hard to look decades younger. 例句：Everyone at the party could tell she was mutton dressed as lamb, showing up in a teeny crop top and platform boots that looked totally out of place on her. 翻译：派对上所有人都看得出来她是“老来俏”，穿着迷你露脐上衣和厚底靴出现，这身打扮在她身上显得格格不入。

definitionCn: 我的错——都怪我。
englishDefinition: My mistake - I'm to blame.
example: My bad for forgetting to bring the printed meeting handouts to the client call this morning.
exampleTranslation: 今早忘了把打印好的会议资料带到客户电话会议上，是我的错。
origin: 源自美式口语，原指承认自身过错，现日常用于为失误致歉，表“我的错”。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，礼貌中性，无褒贬，用于日常向熟人致歉，不适合正式书面或严肃致歉场景。 场景考察：情景：你在图书馆不小心碰掉了同学放在桌边的笔记本，纸张散落一地，你连忙捡起并向对方致歉。 例句：My bad—I didn't mean to knock your notebook off the table. 翻译：我的错——我不是故意把你的笔记本从桌子上碰掉的。

definitionCn: 我的丈夫或我的妻子。
englishDefinition: My husband or my wife.
example: I'm heading out for a quick coffee run — do you want anything, or should I grab something for your better half too?
exampleTranslation: 我正要出去快速买杯咖啡——你想要点什么吗，还是我也顺便给你另一半带点什么？
origin: 源自16世纪，指配偶，将伴侣视作自身更优秀的另一半，表亲昵。
note: 口语化亲昵表达，用于称呼配偶，褒义，非正式场合使用，正式场合慎用，避免对非配偶使用。 场景考察：情景：周末你和朋友在咖啡馆闲聊，朋友问你周末打算怎么安排，你笑着回答要陪另一半去逛新开的文创市集。 例句：I'm going to the new cultural and creative market with my better half this weekend. 翻译：我这周末要和我的另一半去逛新开的文创市集。

definitionCn: 让人感到愉悦的事物或人。
englishDefinition: Something or someone that one finds pleasing.
example: This cozy little café with soft jazz playing in the background is just my cup of tea.
exampleTranslation: 这家放着轻柔爵士乐的温馨小咖啡馆正合我心意。
origin: 源自19世纪英国，因茶普及，用“合口味的茶”喻指喜爱的人或事物。
note: 口语非正式，表喜好，褒义，礼貌，用于日常闲聊，勿在正式场合使用。 场景考察：情景：周末你和朋友逛市集，朋友问你更喜欢手工陶瓷杯还是印花帆布包，你想表达手工陶瓷杯才是你喜欢的类型。 例句：This hand-painted ceramic cup with little rabbit patterns is really my cup of tea. 翻译：这个印着小兔子图案的手绘陶瓷杯可真对我的胃口。

definitionCn: “我的杯满溢”的意思是“我拥有的已远超自身所需”。
englishDefinition: 'My cup runneth over' means 'I have more than enough for my needs'.
example: After receiving the unexpected bonus and warm wishes from all her friends, she felt like her cup runneth over with joy.
exampleTranslation: 在收到意外的奖金以及所有朋友的暖心祝福后，她觉得自己的幸福满得快要溢出来了。
origin: 源自《圣经·诗篇》，原指上帝赐福满溢，后喻所得远超所需，心怀感恩。
note: 口语化表达，带感恩满足的褒义色彩，适用于亲友闲聊、日常分享，正式场合慎用，勿用于炫耀。 场景考察：情景：你刚结束期末周回到家，发现室友为你准备了一桌子你爱吃的菜，还有你念叨了好久的新耳机作为惊喜，你看着满桌的心意忍不住感慨。 例句：Looking at the home-cooked meal on the table and the new headphones I’d been wanting for months, I sighed and said, “My cup runneth over.” 翻译：看着桌上的家常菜和我念叨了好几个月的新耳机，我叹了口气说道：“我真是幸福得不能再幸福了。”

definitionCn: 表示惊讶的感叹语。
englishDefinition: An exclamation of surprise.
example: "My giddy aunt, I can't believe you just won the regional baking competition!"
exampleTranslation: “哎呀，真没想到你居然赢了地区烘焙大赛！”
origin: 源自19世纪英国口语，表惊讶，无明确典故，为随性感叹语。
note: 英式口语感叹语，表惊讶，语气轻松无褒贬，非正式场合使用，对亲友熟人皆可，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你正准备出门上学，突然发现自己忘带书包，而书包里装着今天要交的期末论文，你忍不住惊呼出声。 例句：My giddy aunt! I left my bag at home, and my final paper is in it! 翻译：哎呀！我把书包落家里了，我的期末论文还在里面呢！

definitionCn: 一种强烈情感的表达，通常是感激、爱或喜悦，将心描绘成一个满溢的容器。
englishDefinition: An expression of overwhelming emotion, most often gratitude, love, or joy, picturing the heart as a vessel filled to the brim.
example: After watching my daughter graduate from college, I felt like my heart is full and I couldn't stop smiling.
exampleTranslation: 看着女儿大学毕业后，我内心满是感慨，忍不住一直微笑。
origin: 将心喻为容器，满溢时形容强烈的感激、爱意或喜悦之情。
note: 口语化表达，多用于亲友间抒发强烈的感激、爱意或喜悦，偏褒义，不适合正式场合。 场景考察：情景：你在外求学多年后回到家，推开门看到父母早已备好你最爱吃的饭菜，正笑着等你进门。 例句：Seeing my parents waiting for me at the door with all my favorite dishes, my heart is full. 翻译：看到父母带着我所有爱吃的菜在门口等我，我心里满是感动。

definitionCn: 一种故作谦虚的自谦说法，用来指代自己的家，在欢迎客人时几乎总是带着眨眼的神态说出来。
englishDefinition: A mock-modest way of referring to your own home, almost always said with a wink when welcoming guests.
example: "Welcome to my humble abode—please, come in and make yourselves at home!"
exampleTranslation: “欢迎来到我的寒舍——快请进，别拘束！”
origin: 源自英语，以自谦口吻戏称自家，迎客时带戏谑意味。
note: 口语化谦辞，带玩笑感，用于迎客时自谦称自家，非正式场合，对熟人或客人使用，无贬义。 场景考察：情景：周末你邀请许久未见的大学室友来家里做客，你提前收拾好了客厅，还准备了她最爱喝的果茶，门铃响起时你打开门，笑着对刚到的室友打招呼。 例句："Welcome to my humble abode! I've brewed your favorite peach oolong and set out the strawberry mochi you mentioned last week." 翻译：“欢迎来到我的寒舍呀！我泡了你最爱的蜜桃乌龙，还摆上了你上周提过的草莓麻薯。”

definitionCn: 我和我的丈夫很高兴欢迎各位前来参加我们的银婚纪念庆典。
englishDefinition: This turn of phrase has often been used by Queen Elizabeth II in public speeches. The Queen married the Duke of Edinburgh (formerly Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark) on 20 November 1947. Since that day he has been resigned to walking a few paces behind her in public. Putting the husband first in 'my husband and I' was a device used to indicate the dominance of the male in marriage - Elizabeth emphasized this by using the traditional 'honour and obey' pledge at her wedding. The stilted 'my husband and I' became rather out of touch with modern thoughts about marriage and was satirized in the UK in the 1960s and onwards. The Queen now rarely, if ever, uses the phrase. Her consciousness of the notoriety of the phrase was tacitly acknowledged when she wheeled it out for a late airing in her speech at Guildhall, London in November 1972, on the occasion of her 25th wedding anniversary: "I think that everybody really will concede that on this, of all days, I should begin my speech with the words 'My husband and I'".
example: My grandmother still insists on saying "my husband and I" when talking about her late spouse, even though most people her age have long since dropped that old-fashioned turn of phrase.
exampleTranslation: 我祖母在谈论她已故的配偶时，仍然坚持说“我丈夫和我”，即使她那个年纪的大多数人早就不再使用这种老式的说法了。
origin: 源自英女王伊丽莎白二世公开演讲，用以凸显婚姻中男性主导地位，后因脱离现代婚姻观念遭讽刺。
note: 正式场合用语，曾为英女王公开演讲常用，体现传统婚姻男权观念，现显过时，不宜日常使用。 场景考察：情景：在结婚25周年的晚宴上，伊丽莎白二世女王准备发表致辞，她想要用一句大家熟悉的、能体现王室传统的开场白来引出自己的讲话。 例句：My husband and I are delighted to welcome you all to this celebration of our Silver Wedding anniversary.

definitionCn: 一个人的视觉记忆或想象力。
englishDefinition: One's visual memory or imagination.
example: When I close my eyes and picture my childhood home, I can still see every detail of the living room in my mind's eye.
exampleTranslation: 当我闭上眼睛回想童年的家时，我依然能在脑海中清晰地看到客厅的每一个细节。
origin: 源自莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》，指人脑中的视觉记忆与想象。
note: 用于书面或口语描述想象、回忆画面，中性表达，无褒贬，适用于日常交流、写作等场景。 场景考察：情景：美术课上老师让大家凭记忆画出自己家的客厅，你闭着眼睛在脑海里勾勒出沙发、茶几和墙上的全家福的样子。 例句：I pictured my cozy living room in my mind's eye before starting to draw it for art class. 翻译：在美术课上开始画我舒适的客厅之前，我先在脑海里勾勒出了它的样子。

definitionCn: 对朋友的亲昵称呼。
englishDefinition: Affectionate term for a friend.
example: I've known my old china for over twenty years, and we still meet for a pint every Friday after work.
exampleTranslation: 我认识我的老伙计已经二十多年了，我们仍然每周五下班后都会聚在一起喝一杯。
origin: 源自伦敦押韵俚语，china plate谐音mate，代指好友，是对朋友的亲昵称呼。
note: 英式口语俚语，表亲昵，仅用于熟人好友间，正式场合或对陌生人使用会显得唐突失礼。 场景考察：情景：你和相识多年的死党在常去的咖啡馆碰面，对方刚帮你带了你最爱的冰美式，你笑着拍了拍他的肩膀打招呼。 例句：Hey, my old china, thanks for grabbing my usual drink for me on such a cold morning! 翻译：嘿，老伙计，谢谢你在这么冷的早上帮我带了我常喝的饮品！

definitionCn: 对妻子的亲昵称呼。
englishDefinition: An affectionate term for wife.
example: Whenever I'm feeling down, my old Dutch always knows how to cheer me up with a warm cup of tea and a listening ear.
exampleTranslation: 每当我情绪低落时，我的老伴总会泡上一杯热茶，耐心听我倾诉，知道怎么让我振作起来。
origin: 源自航海俚语，Dutch代指妻子，因荷兰人重视家庭，引申为对妻子的亲昵称呼。
note: 英式口语俚语，亲昵称呼妻子，仅用于夫妻间非正式场合，语气亲昵，无贬义，不适用于正式场合或他人配偶。 场景考察：情景：周末傍晚，你和好友在街边的小酒馆闲聊，他指着身边正笑着递给他一杯热咖啡的妻子，满脸温柔地向你介绍。 例句：He introduced his wife to me with a smile, saying, "This is my old Dutch, we've been through so much together." 翻译：他笑着向我介绍他的妻子，说道：“这是我的老伴，我们一起经历了太多。”

definitionCn: 成语“my way or the highway”强烈表达了“你要么接受，要么拉倒”的观点。
englishDefinition: The idiom 'my way or the highway' forcefully expresses the view that 'you can take it or leave it'.
example: If you don't agree with my plan for the project, you can find another team to work with—it's my way or the highway.
exampleTranslation: 如果你不认同我这个项目的方案，你可以找别的团队合作——要么按我的来，要么走人。
origin: 源自20世纪美国，原指不按要求做事就得走人，现喻强硬要求服从。
note: 口语俚语，语气强硬带命令感，多用于日常争执，不适合正式场合，对长辈或上级使用易引发冲突。 场景考察：情景：一家创业公司的创始人在团队会议上拍板敲定了产品上线时间，面对成员提出的延期申请，他态度坚决地表明了自己的立场。 例句：When the team asked for a two-week extension on the project deadline, the CEO said, "My way or the highway—we launch on the 15th, no exceptions." 翻译：当团队要求将项目截止日期延长两周时，首席执行官说：“要么按我的方式来，要么就走人——我们15号上线，没有例外。” ## N

definitionCn: 把一件事做得极其出色，精准达成预期目标。
englishDefinition: To do something extremely well, achieving exactly the intended result.
example: She nailed it in her job interview and got the offer on the spot.
exampleTranslation: 她在求职面试中表现得极为出色，当场就拿到了录用通知。
origin: 源自钉钉子，精准钉入即达预期，喻指完美达成目标。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，褒义，用于夸赞他人出色完成任务，礼貌得体，无冒犯性。 场景考察：情景：你花了整整一周时间反复练习期末英语口语展示，对着镜子调整发音、打磨手势，正式上台时全程流畅自然，完全没有卡顿忘词，结束后台下响起了热烈的掌声。 例句：You totally nailed your final English presentation! 翻译：你这次期末英语口语展示完成得太出色了！

word: Nail your colours to the mast
definitionCn: 坚定地表达个人的观点与信念，同时表明自己会将这些信念坚持到底的决心。
englishDefinition: To defiantly display one's opinions and beliefs. Also, to show one's intention to hold on to those beliefs until the end.
example: After the scandal broke, the senator refused to back down from his controversial policy, choosing to nail his colours to the mast and defend his stance to the very end.
exampleTranslation: 丑闻曝光后，这位参议员拒绝在自己备受争议的政策上退让，选择公开表明立场，并坚持到底为自己的态度辩护。
origin: 源自航海习俗，钉牢旗帜于桅杆以示绝不投降，喻坚定立场、绝不妥协。
note: 该俚语为口语化表达，褒义，指坚定公开立场、绝不妥协，适用于日常非正式交流，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：在学校的辩论赛上，你作为正方一辩，面对反方提出的多个刁钻问题，依然坚定地表明自己支持“中学生应该参与校园公共事务管理”的立场，不肯退让半步。 例句：During the debate, she nailed her colours to the mast and insisted that students should have a say in school management. 翻译：在辩论赛中，她明确表明自己的立场，坚持认为学生应该在学校管理中有发言权。

definitionCn: 幼稚且多愁善感。
englishDefinition: Childish and weakly sentimental.
example: Stop being so namby-pamby and tell me exactly what you think of my new plan.
exampleTranslation: 别这么婆婆妈妈的，直接告诉我你觉得我的新计划怎么样。
origin: 源自18世纪诗人安布罗斯·菲利普斯的幼稚诗作，后泛指多愁善感、软弱幼稚的人或事物。
note: 口语贬义词，形容人幼稚多愁善感，非正式场合使用，对长辈或正式交流慎用，避免冒犯他人。 场景考察：情景：小组项目讨论时，有人提出要给流浪动物救助站设计宣传海报，却因为怕被同学笑话“太矫情”，迟迟不敢说出自己想在海报上印软萌小猫照片的想法，你可以用这个俚语评价这种没主见、多愁善感的状态。 例句：Stop being so namby-pamby and just tell your group members that you want to include cute cat photos on the poster for the animal shelter! 翻译：别这么没主见、多愁善感了，直接告诉你的组员，你想在动物救助站的海报上放可爱的猫咪照片吧！

definitionCn: 公布某个人或群体在某一反社会行为中应承担的责任，以使其蒙羞并悔悟。
englishDefinition: The publication of the identity of a person or group that is culpable in some anti-social act in order to shame them into remorse.
example: Many communities choose to name and shame drunk drivers to deter others from making the same dangerous choice.
exampleTranslation: 许多社区会公开酒驾者的身份以使其蒙羞，从而震慑其他人不要做出同样危险的选择。
origin: 源自公开披露作恶者身份，以羞辱促其悔悟的社会惩戒做法。
note: 口语化表达，多用于公开曝光不良行为者以促其悔悟，语气直接，带明确负面指向，不适合正式礼貌场合。 场景考察：情景：社区里有居民多次在深夜制造噪音，影响邻居休息，物业决定在小区公告栏公示这类违规住户的姓名和行为，督促他们改正。 例句：The property management decided to name and shame residents who repeatedly violated the noise regulations. 翻译：物业决定点名批评那些屡次违反噪音规定的住户。

definitionCn: “恶劣、粗野且短暂”是17世纪的一个短语，用来描述人类处于战争状态时的生活。
englishDefinition: 'Nasty, brutish and short' is a 17th century phrase describing the life of mankind when in a state of war.
example: Without strong social institutions, life in the lawless frontier was often nasty, brutish and short.
exampleTranslation: 如果没有完善的社会制度，在无法无天的边疆地区的生活往往是恶劣、野蛮且短暂的。
origin: 源自霍布斯《利维坦》，形容自然状态下人的生活恶劣、野蛮、短暂。
note: 源自霍布斯，书面正式用语，无褒贬，用于描述恶劣、粗野且短暂的生存状态，不用于日常口语。 场景考察：情景：你和朋友聊起最近刚结束的、连轴转的期末周，每天泡图书馆复习到凌晨，还要赶各种小组作业，连好好吃顿饭的时间都没有，整个人累到脱力，你想用这个俚语形容这段糟糕的经历。 例句："My final exam week was absolutely nasty, brutish and short — I barely slept, survived on instant noodles, and was so relieved when it was finally over." 翻译：“我的期末周简直是又糟又累还难熬——我几乎没怎么睡，靠泡面续命，终于熬过去的时候我整个人都松了口气。”

definitionCn: “先天还是后天”这一说法常被用来指代一场争论，即在塑造一个人的特质、行为和发展方面，遗传（先天）与教养和环境（后天）的相对重要性之争。
englishDefinition: The expression 'nature or nurture' is often used to refer to the debate about the relative importance of genetics (nature) versus upbringing and environment (nurture) in shaping an individual's traits, behaviour and development.
example: The debate over whether intelligence is primarily determined by genetics or life experience boils down to the classic nature versus nurture argument.
exampleTranslation: 关于智力主要由基因还是人生经历决定的争论，归根结底就是经典的“先天与后天”之争。
origin: 源自探讨遗传与环境对个体发展影响的经典议题，指先天本性与后天教养之争。
note: 用于讨论遗传与环境对人成长影响的正式学术或公共话题，中性客观，无褒贬，适用于教育、心理等领域的专业交流。 场景考察：情景：你和同学在讨论“为什么有人天生擅长数学，有人却需要靠后天反复练习才能学好”，正好可以用这个俚语来描述这场关于先天基因和后天培养哪个更重要的讨论。 例句：The debate over whether a person's intelligence is mostly inherited or shaped by their family and schooling is a classic example of nature versus nurture. 翻译：关于一个人的智力主要是先天遗传还是由家庭和学校教育塑造的争论，是典型的先天与后天之争。

word: Ne'er cast a clout till May be out
phonetic: /neɪ kɑːst ə klaʊt tɪl meɪ biː aʊt/
definitionCn: “‘ne'er cast a clout……’的意思就是‘千万别把你的[冬季保暖]衣物收起来……’。”
englishDefinition: 'ne'er cast a clout...' simply means 'never discard your [warm winter] clothing...'.
example: My grandma always reminds me of the old saying "Ne'er cast a clout till May be out" when I want to put away my thick coat in early spring.
exampleTranslation: 每当我想在早春收起厚外套时，奶奶总会提醒我那句老话“未出五月莫脱衣”。
origin: 英国古谚，源自气候经验，告诫五月未过勿急脱冬衣，防倒春寒着凉。
note: 英式口语谚语，非正式，无褒贬，提醒勿过早脱冬衣，适用于日常闲聊，勿用于正式文书。 场景考察：情景：四月末的清晨，你收拾换季衣物时想把厚外套收进储物箱，奶奶拦住你提醒这句英国老谚语，说五月还没结束前别太早收起保暖衣物。 例句：Ne'er cast a clout till May be out, so don't put away your thick coat yet—there may still be a few chilly mornings left this spring. 翻译：未出五月别收厚衣，所以先别把厚外套收起来——今年春天可能还会有几个寒冷的清晨。

definitionCn: 一个一无是处的人。
englishDefinition: A worthless, good for nothing person.
example: The old town gossip claimed that the mysterious stranger who’d just moved into the abandoned cottage on the hill was a ne’er do well who’d been run out of three neighboring counties for skipping out on his debts.
exampleTranslation: 镇上的老八卦说，刚搬进山上那间废弃小屋的神秘陌生人是个游手好闲的废物，因为躲债已经被周边三个县赶出来过了。
origin: 源自18世纪苏格兰，指游手好闲、一无是处的人，含贬义。
note: 口语俚语，带贬义，指一无是处的人，仅用于非正式场合，对他人使用不礼貌。 场景考察：情景：社区里有个整天游手好闲、靠亲戚接济过活的人，邻居们提起他时总忍不住摇头叹气。 例句：The neighbors all avoid that ne'er-do-well who never holds down a job and always borrows money from people around him. 翻译：邻居们都躲着那个游手好闲的人，他从来没有一份稳定的工作，还总跟身边的人借钱。

definitionCn: 刚好处于可接受的边缘，尤其是在性道德方面。
englishDefinition: Just at the limit of acceptability, especially regarding sexual morals.
example: The comedian’s near-the-knuckle jokes about relationships made some audience members shift uncomfortably in their seats.
exampleTranslation: 这位喜剧演员关于两性关系的擦边笑话让一些观众在座位上坐立难安。
origin: 源自英国俚语，knuckle指指关节，喻指贴近底线，尤指性道德方面接近可接受的极限。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，略带冒犯，不宜对陌生人或正式场合使用，指内容接近可接受底线，尤涉性道德。 场景考察：情景：在大学创意写作课上，老师点评学生提交的短篇小说，指出其中一段描写情侣互动的情节尺度过于贴近公序良俗的边界，很容易引发读者的不适。 例句：The professor warned the student that the scene he wrote in his short story was near the knuckle and might make some readers feel uncomfortable. 翻译：教授提醒这名学生，他在短篇小说里写的那段情节尺度过于贴近公序良俗的边界，可能会让部分读者感到不适。

word: Necessity is the mother of invention
definitionCn: 由于自动浇水装置在科学展开幕前两天坏了，约翰不得不用旧塑料瓶和橡皮筋做了一个新的。常言道，需求是发明之母。
englishDefinition: Other Quotations Difficult situations inspire ingenious solutions.
example: When the power went out during the camping trip, we had to build a makeshift shelter from fallen branches and old tarps—after all, necessity is the mother of invention.
exampleTranslation: 露营途中突然停电，我们只能用掉落的树枝和旧防水布搭了个临时庇护所——毕竟需求是发明之母。
origin: 出自柏拉图《理想国》，指需求催生创造，困境能激发人的巧思与发明。
note: 适用于口语或书面，中性无褒贬，可用于鼓励他人或评论困境催生创意，避免用于严肃正式公文。 场景考察：情景：学校的科学展即将开幕，你需要制作一个能自动给盆栽浇水的装置，但手头没有现成的自动浇水零件，也没时间去商店采购。 例句：Since the automatic watering system broke two days before the science fair, John had to build a new one from old plastic bottles and rubber bands. As they say, necessity is the mother of invention.

definitionCn: 社区、地区或区域..
englishDefinition: Neighbourhood, region or area..
example: I ran into an old classmate while hiking in my neck of the woods last weekend.
exampleTranslation: 上周末我在我家附近的地方徒步时，偶遇了一位老同学。
origin: 源自旧时北美林区以树木方位划分区域的说法，现指某一地区或邻近地带。
note: 口语化表达，无褒贬，指某地区/街区，日常闲聊适用，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你在咖啡馆偶遇一位来自你家乡的老朋友，对方惊喜地问你怎么会出现在这里。例句："What are you doing in this neck of the woods?"翻译："你怎么会在这一带？"

definitionCn: Needs must 的意思是，必要性让你别无选择，所以一件不受欢迎的事无论如何都会被完成。
englishDefinition: Needs must means that necessity leaves you no choice, so an unwelcome thing gets done anyway.
example: When the car broke down on the highway with no mechanic in sight, needs must — I called my neighbor to come pick me up even though I hated asking for help.
exampleTranslation: 汽车在高速公路上抛锚了，附近连个修车工都没有，实在是没办法——尽管我很讨厌求人，还是打电话叫邻居来接我了。
origin: 源自古英语谚语，指迫于情势不得不做不愿做的事，强调必要性压倒个人意愿。
note: Needs must表无奈之举，偏口语，中性，无褒贬，适用于熟人闲聊，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你原本计划周末宅家追剧，可室友突然急性肠胃炎需要有人陪同去医院，你虽然满心不情愿，还是只能放下手头的事陪室友就诊。 例句：Needs must, so I canceled my movie plans and accompanied my sick roommate to the hospital. 翻译：实在是没办法，我只好取消了看电影的计划，陪生病的室友去了医院。

word: Neither a borrower nor a lender be
phonetic: /ˈnaɪðə ə ˈbɒrəʊə nɔː ə ˈlendə biː/
definitionCn: 字面意思。
englishDefinition: Literal meaning.
example: My dad always told me to follow the old saying "Neither a borrower nor a lender be", so I never lend money to friends or borrow from them.
exampleTranslation: 我爸爸总是告诉我要遵循那句老话“既不要向人借钱，也不要借钱给人”，所以我从不借钱给朋友，也不向他们借钱。
origin: 出自《哈姆雷特》波洛涅斯劝子语，告诫勿借贷，免伤财失友。
note: 正式劝诫语，礼貌中性，多用于告诫他人勿借贷，不直接用于熟人日常口语。 场景考察：情景：期末周结束后，你发现同寝室的室友既没有向其他同学借复习笔记，也没有把自己的课堂笔记借给别人，全程独立完成了所有备考任务。 例句：My roommate followed the old saying "neither a borrower nor a lender be" during finals week, studying entirely on her own without borrowing notes from anyone or lending hers out. 翻译：我的室友在期末周期间恪守“既不向人借，也不借与人”的古训，全程独立学习，既没有向任何人借笔记，也没有把自己的笔记借给别人。

definitionCn: 两种方式都无关紧要。
englishDefinition: Of no consequence either one way or the other.
example: Whether we have pizza or burgers for lunch is neither here nor there, as long as we get something to eat before the meeting starts.
exampleTranslation: 我们午餐吃披萨还是汉堡都无关紧要，只要在会议开始前能吃上东西就行。
origin: 源自莎剧《威尼斯商人》，指无关紧要、不影响结果的事物。
note: 口语化表达，非正式场合使用，中性无褒贬，用于说明某事物无关紧要，不适合正式文书或严肃沟通场景。 场景考察：情景：你和朋友在餐厅纠结选靠窗还是靠门的座位，朋友说两个位置视野差不多，选哪个都不影响用餐体验。 例句：Whether we sit by the window or the door is neither here nor there, since the food tastes the same either way. 翻译：我们坐靠窗还是靠门的位置都无关紧要，反正食物的味道是一样的。

definitionCn: 非常勇敢、自信且有胆识，即使在压力特别大的情况下，也能保持沉着冷静的态度。
englishDefinition: Very brave, confident and courageous, with a calm and collected demeanour, even in particularly stressful situations.
example: Even when the entire audience was staring at her during the national speech contest, she stood on the stage with nerves of steel, delivering her speech smoothly without a single stutter.
exampleTranslation: 即使在全国演讲比赛中全场观众都注视着她，她依然临危不乱地站在台上，流畅地完成了演讲，没有出现一次结巴。
origin: 源自钢铁坚固意象，喻指高压下仍能保持镇定、果敢无畏的心理素质。
note: 口语褒义俚语，用于夸赞他人高压下仍沉着勇敢，礼貌得体，不适用于正式文书。 场景考察：情景：学校年度英语演讲比赛的决赛现场，台下坐满了师生评委，参赛选手小林站在聚光灯下，全程没有丝毫慌乱，流畅地完成了整场演讲。 例句：Even though she was about to deliver a speech to hundreds of people, she had nerves of steel and never showed a single sign of anxiety. 翻译：尽管她要给数百人做演讲，她却有着钢铁般的意志，丝毫没有表现出焦虑的迹象。

definitionCn: 一种强烈的方式来表示同意某人刚才所说的话完全正确。
englishDefinition: An emphatic way of agreeing that what someone has just said is exactly right.
example: "When my friend said that nothing beats a hot cup of tea on a rainy day, I nodded and said, 'Never a truer word spoken.'"
exampleTranslation: "当我的朋友说下雨天没有什么比一杯热茶更治愈时，我点头说道：‘说得太对了。’"
origin: 源自英语日常口语，用于强烈认同他人所言完全正确，无特殊历史典故。
note: 口语非正式场合，表强烈认同，褒义，礼貌得体，适用于赞同他人观点时，勿用于正式文书。 场景考察：情景：你和好友刚结束一场连续加班两周的项目，瘫在公司楼下的长椅上，好友长舒一口气说“我真觉得咱们这阵子连轴转的日子快把人熬垮了”，你想用这句俚语表达完全认同他的感受。 例句："Never a truer word spoken — I’ve barely had a full night’s sleep in the last two weeks." 翻译：“说得太对了——这两周我几乎就没睡过一个整觉。”

word: Never give a sucker an even break
phonetic: /ˈnevə ɡɪv ə ˈsʌkər ən ˈiːv(ə)n breɪk/
definitionCn: 字面意思，但通常用于制造喜剧效果。
englishDefinition: Literal meaning, but usually used for comic effect.
example: When the con artist saw the tourist fall for his obvious scam, he grinned and muttered, "Never give a sucker an even break."
exampleTranslation: 当这个骗子看到游客轻易上了他那拙劣骗局的当时，他咧嘴一笑，低声说道：“绝不能给傻瓜可乘之机。”
origin: 源自美国俚语，指别给易受骗者公平机会，常带戏谑喜剧效果。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，带嘲讽贬义，仅用于熟人玩笑，勿对陌生人或正式场合使用，避免冒犯他人。 场景考察：情景：You're at a local fair, watching a seasoned con artist pretend to be a friendly stranger while he secretly rigs a simple ring-toss game to cheat a nervous first-time player out of their cash. 例句：The grinning carnival barker running the rigged ring-toss booth never gave a wide-eyed tourist an even break, letting them waste all their cash on impossible throws before they realized they'd been scammed. 翻译：那个经营着作弊套圈摊位、咧嘴笑着的嘉年华摊主从来不给毫无戒心的游客任何公平机会，任由他们在根本不可能投中的项目上浪费光所有现金，之后才意识到自己被骗了。

definitionCn: 约翰·路易斯合伙公司自20世纪20年代起使用的口号。
englishDefinition: The slogan of the John Lewis Partnership from the 1920s.
example: When shopping for home appliances, many customers trust John Lewis because of its long-standing "never knowingly undersold" promise, which means they will not be beaten on price by any competitor.
exampleTranslation: 购买家电时，许多顾客信任约翰·路易斯，因为它长期秉持“绝不故意售价高于同行”的承诺，这意味着它的价格不会输给任何竞争对手。
origin: 约翰·路易斯1920年代起使用的口号，承诺不故意卖高价，主打诚信定价。
note: 约翰·路易斯品牌口号，表“绝不故意低价售劣”，仅作品牌宣传，非日常俚语，无褒贬，不用于普通对话。 场景考察：情景：你和朋友逛完市中心的百货商场，朋友拿起一件标价偏高的羊毛大衣，吐槽说这家店的东西比网上贵不少，你想起这家店是英国老牌百货，一直有承诺绝不卖得比别家贵的招牌口号，于是你用这个俚语跟朋友解释这家店的定价原则。 例句：As a department store famous for its long-standing commitment to "never knowingly undersold", John Lewis will match the price of any identical product sold by its high street competitors. 翻译：作为一家以长期践行“绝不故意售价高于同行”承诺而闻名的百货公司，约翰·刘易斯会对其商业街竞争对手售卖的任何同款产品实行价格匹配。

definitionCn: 差异极大、毫无结合可能的两种事物。
englishDefinition: Two things which are so different as to have no opportunity to unite.
example: After years of arguing about politics, they finally accepted that their views were never the twain shall meet.
exampleTranslation: 经过多年的政治争论，他们终于接受了彼此的观点截然不同、无法达成一致的事实。
origin: 源自吉卜力《营房谣》，喻指差异极大、永无交集的双方。
note: 口语化表达，带调侃意味，用于形容差异极大、绝无交集的两类人或事物，不适合正式场合，无冒犯性。 场景考察：情景：你正在和朋友讨论性格截然相反的两个人——一个是热爱户外探险、周末总去徒步露营的运动达人，另一个是喜欢宅家看书、连下楼取快递都嫌麻烦的安静书虫，两人的生活习惯几乎没有任何交集。 例句：My adventurous roommate who climbs mountains every weekend and my best friend who never leaves her apartment except to go to work are like never the twain shall meet. 翻译：我那每个周末都去爬山的爱冒险的室友，和我那个除了上班从不出门的好朋友，简直是两个完全不可能有交集的人。

definitionCn: 一个乌托邦式的梦境。
englishDefinition: A utopian dreamland.
example: After a long week of exams, she escaped to her own Never-Never land by curling up with a fantasy novel and a cup of hot cocoa.
exampleTranslation: 经过整整一周的考试，她蜷在沙发上，捧着一本奇幻小说，喝着热可可，躲进了属于自己的梦幻乌托邦。
origin: 源自詹姆斯·巴里《彼得·潘》，指孩童幻想的永无岛，喻脱离现实的乌托邦。
note: 口语俚语，带戏谑或批评色彩，指脱离现实的空想境地，不宜用于正式场合，避免对他人使用。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友总说要等攒够钱就立刻辞职环游世界，却迟迟不肯开始存钱，也不肯规划行程，一直沉浸在不切实际的幻想里。 例句：My friend keeps saying he'll quit his job and travel the world once he saves enough money, but he never actually starts saving or planning—he's just living in Never-Never land. 翻译：我的朋友总说等攒够钱就辞职环游世界，但他既不开始存钱也不规划行程——他只是活在不切实际的幻想里。

definitionCn: 这些话总是被用作反驳先前陈述事实的反论点。
englishDefinition: These words always appear as the counter argument to some earlier stated fact.
example: Nevertheless, the initial survey results were promising, these words always appear as the counter argument to some earlier stated fact.
exampleTranslation: 尽管如此，最初的调查结果是令人鼓舞的，这些词总是作为对先前陈述事实的反驳出现。
origin: 源自日常英语表达，表转折，常用来反驳或修正前文已陈述的事实。
note: 正式书面语，中性转折，礼貌得体，用于反驳前文事实，不针对个人，适用于论述、报告等正式语境。 场景考察：情景：你和朋友讨论周末出游计划，朋友说天气预报显示周六大概率是大晴天，非常适合去郊外徒步，你补充说虽然天气看起来不错，但你上周刚扭伤脚踝，暂时没法走太远的山路。 例句：Nevertheless, I cannot go hiking with you this weekend because I sprained my ankle last week. 翻译：尽管如此，我这周末没法和你一起去徒步，因为我上周扭伤了脚踝。

definitionCn: 一个新来到某个地区或加入某个年轻朋友圈的人。
englishDefinition: A new arrival in an area or in a group of young friends.
example: As the new kid on the block at the high school, he was invited to join the popular group of seniors hanging out at the local mall.
exampleTranslation: 作为高中里新来的家伙，他被邀请加入了在当地商场闲逛的那群受欢迎的高年级学生。
origin: 源自北美街区邻里文化，指新搬来的年轻人，后泛指群体中新加入的成员。
note: 口语俚语，中性偏褒，指新来的人或事物，非正式场合使用，避免用于正式文书或严肃评价。 场景考察：情景：刚转学到新班级的同学还没认识其他伙伴，课间独自坐在座位上翻看课本。 例句：As the new kid on the block, he didn't know anyone at his new school. 翻译：作为新来的人，他在新学校里谁也不认识。

definitionCn: 极短的时间，用于描述某事发生的速度快得惊人。
englishDefinition: A very short space of time, used to describe something happening with startling speed.
example: If you need me to run to the corner store for a bottle of water, I can do it in a New York minute.
exampleTranslation: 如果你需要我去街角便利店买瓶水，我一眨眼就能跑个来回。
origin: 源自美式英语，形容纽约生活节奏快，指极短的瞬间。
note: 口语俚语，无褒贬，适用于日常非正式场合，形容极短时间内发生的事，正式文书不宜使用。 场景考察：情景：你正和朋友在纽约街头赶时间去看一场期待已久的百老汇演出，眼看就要迟到，朋友却突然说他能在极短时间内买到路边的热咖啡，你可以用这个俚语描述他的速度。 例句：My friend can grab a cup of hot coffee from the street vendor in a New York minute when we are in a rush to catch the Broadway show. 翻译：当我们赶时间去看百老汇演出时，我朋友能在一瞬间从街头小贩那里买到一杯热咖啡。

definitionCn: 深夜仍活跃的人。
englishDefinition: A person who is active late at night.
example: As a night owl, she often gets her best writing done after midnight when the house is quiet.
exampleTranslation: 作为一个夜猫子，她常常在午夜之后、屋子安静下来时写出最好的作品。
origin: 源自猫头鹰夜行习性，喻指习惯熬夜、深夜仍保持活跃的人。
note: 口语俚语，中性无褒贬，可用于日常闲聊，描述熬夜活跃的人，不适合正式文书，无冒犯性。 场景考察：情景：周末的图书馆自习区里，大部分同学都在傍晚收拾东西准备回宿舍休息，只有靠窗的男生小林还在对着电脑专注地写课程论文，窗外的天色从深灰变成全黑，走廊的灯都陆续亮了起来，他丝毫没有要停下的意思。 例句：My roommate is a real night owl who always stays up until 2 a.m. to finish her design assignments. 翻译：我的室友是个不折不扣的夜猫子，她总是熬到凌晨两点才完成她的设计作业。

definitionCn: 人类粪便的委婉说法。
englishDefinition: Euphemism for human faeces.
example: In some historical agricultural texts, night soil was collected from urban households and used as fertilizer for nearby farmlands.
exampleTranslation: 在一些历史农业文献中，人粪尿会从城市住户家中被收集起来，用作附近农田的肥料。
origin: 源自旧时夜间以灯照明收集人粪作肥料的行业，是对人粪的委婉说法。
note: 委婉语，用于指代人类粪便，常见于农业、卫生或历史语境，语气正式，无褒贬，避免直接提及排泄物。 场景考察：情景：一位历史老师正在给学生讲解19世纪城市的卫生状况，提到当时的清洁工常会在夜间收集一种被委婉称为“Night soil”的物质，用作农田肥料。 例句：In the 1800s, farmers often used night soil as a natural fertilizer for their crops. 翻译：在19世纪，农民常把人粪尿（夜肥）用作农作物的天然肥料。

definitionCn: 一种新奇事物，几天后就失去了吸引力。
englishDefinition: A novelty that loses its appeal after a few days.
example: The viral dance trend was a nine days' wonder, forgotten by most people within a week.
exampleTranslation: 这个爆火的舞蹈潮流只是昙花一现，不到一周就被大多数人遗忘了。
origin: 源自莎士比亚戏剧，指仅短期新奇、很快便无人关注的人或事物。
note: 口语化表达，略带贬义，适用于非正式场合，用于调侃热度短暂的人或事物，不宜用于正式文书或严肃评价。 场景考察：情景：你的室友上周兴冲冲买了一台网红家用酸奶机，头两天还每天早起做酸奶发朋友圈，结果新鲜劲过了之后，机器就被塞到橱柜角落再也没碰过，你可以用这个俚语评价这件事。 例句：That fancy yogurt maker my roommate bought was a nine days' wonder—she hasn't touched it since the third day. 翻译：我室友买的那台花哨酸奶机真是个新鲜不了几天的玩意儿——她从第三天起就再也没碰过它。

definitionCn: 朝九晚五指的是许多办公室岗位的标准工作日，从早上九点一直持续到晚上五点，常被用来指代枯燥、重复的日常工作。
englishDefinition: Nine to five describes the standard working day of many office jobs, running from nine in the morning until five in the evening, and is often used to suggest a dull, repetitive routine.
example: After years of working a nine to five desk job, she decided to quit and travel around the world.
exampleTranslation: 在做了多年朝九晚五的办公室工作后，她决定辞职环游世界。
origin: 源自传统办公作息，指朝九晚五的固定工作，常喻枯燥重复的日常。
note: 口语俚语，无褒贬，多用于日常闲聊，描述朝九晚五的常规办公作息，不适合正式文书或严肃职场沟通。 场景考察：情景：刚毕业的大学生林恩拿到了一家互联网公司的全职offer，入职后每天早上9点到公司打卡上班，下午5点准时下班，周末不用加班，她和朋友聊起这份工作时提到了这种固定的办公节奏。 例句：Lynn finally landed a stable nine to five job after graduation, which allows her to pick up her little sister from school every weekday evening. 翻译：林恩毕业后终于找到了一份朝九晚五的稳定工作，这让她每个工作日傍晚都能去接妹妹放学。

definitionCn: 一场势均力敌的比赛或竞赛指的是结果非常接近的比赛。最近，“Nip and tuck”被用作一种整容手术的名称。
englishDefinition: A nip and tuck race race or contest is one with close result. More recently, 'Nip and tuck' has been adopted as the name of a cosmetic surgery procedure.
example: The two runners were nip and tuck for most of the marathon, with neither able to pull ahead until the final stretch.
exampleTranslation: 在马拉松的大部分赛程里，两名选手势均力敌，直到最后冲刺阶段才分出胜负。
origin: 原指势均力敌的竞赛，后被借用作整容手术（拉皮）的代称。
note: 口语，形容比赛势均力敌；正式场合慎用，无褒贬，指整容义需注意语境。 场景考察：情景：校运会100米决赛的最后冲刺阶段，两名选手几乎同时撞线，全程你追我赶难分高下。 例句：The 100-meter final was nip and tuck all the way, with both runners crossing the finish line at almost the same moment. 翻译：这场100米决赛全程势均力敌，两名选手几乎同时撞线。

definitionCn: 把某件事扼杀在萌芽状态，就是在它还处于早期发展阶段时就加以制止。
englishDefinition: To nip something in the bud is to put a stop to it while it is still in its early development.
example: The manager decided to nip the office gossip in the bud before it spread further and affected team morale.
exampleTranslation: 经理决定在办公室流言进一步扩散、影响团队士气之前就将其扼杀在萌芽状态。
origin: 源自园艺，指趁花蕾未开即摘除，喻及早将事物扼杀于萌芽阶段。
note: 通用口语，中性偏积极，无褒贬，适用于各类日常及非正式场合，可对人对事，正式文书中慎用。 场景考察：情景：你发现刚上初中的弟弟最近总偷偷熬夜刷短视频，作业敷衍了事，成绩已经出现下滑苗头，你打算及时制止这个坏习惯，避免它愈演愈烈。 例句：You should nip your younger brother's late-night short-video watching habit in the bud before it seriously affects his schoolwork. 翻译：你应该趁早制止弟弟熬夜刷短视频的习惯，别等它严重影响他的学业。

definitionCn: 因衣物滑落或不合身而意外、通常短暂且局部地露出女性乳头。
englishDefinition: The accidental, usually brief and partial, exposure of a woman's nipple caused by a slipping or ill-fitting garment.
example: The actress had a minor nip slip on the red carpet when her strapless gown shifted slightly during the photo call.
exampleTranslation: 这位女演员在红毯拍照环节，抹胸礼服轻微移位，不慎走光露出了乳头。
origin: 源自欧美娱乐八卦圈，指女性衣物滑落意外短暂露出乳头的走光现象。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，带调侃意味，涉及女性身体，易冒犯，勿用于正式场合或对女性随意使用。 场景考察：情景：A young woman is walking on a windy city street, wearing a loose, thin-strapped camisole. A sudden gust of wind blows the camisole strap off her shoulder, briefly shifting the fabric to expose part of her nipple before she quickly adjusts her clothing. 例句：She had a nip slip when the wind blew her camisole strap off her shoulder, and she quickly pulled her clothing back into place. 翻译：一阵风把她的吊带肩带吹落，她不小心走光露出了乳头，于是赶紧把衣服拉回原位。

definitionCn: 问题的核心；基本要点。这个短语通常以扩展形式“get down to the nitty-gritty”使用。
englishDefinition: The heart of the matter; the basic essentials. The phrase is usually used in the extended form 'get down to the nitty-gritty'.
example: After spending the first hour of the meeting making small talk, the project manager finally asked everyone to get down to the nitty-gritty and discuss the actual budget constraints.
exampleTranslation: 在会议的第一个小时都在闲聊之后，项目经理终于要求大家切入正题，讨论实际的预算限制。
origin: 源自非裔美语，原指黑奴船舱底层污垢，后喻指事物核心本质。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合用，中性无褒贬，指核心实质，多用于熟人或轻松交流，正式文书慎用。 场景考察：情景：小组项目讨论会上，大家已经寒暄完毕、聊完了周末的出游计划，接下来要切入正题敲定最终的项目分工与截止日期。 例句：Now that we've finished the small talk, let's get down to the nitty-gritty and finalize our project timeline. 翻译：既然我们已经闲聊完了，咱们就切入正题，敲定项目的时间线吧。

definitionCn: “no dice”这个表达是对某个提议的拒绝，等同于“不行”。
englishDefinition: The expression 'no dice' is a refusal to accept a proposition - equivalent to 'nothing doing'.
example: I asked my boss if I could take Friday off, but he said no dice because we're short-staffed this week.
exampleTranslation: 我问老板周五能不能请假，但他说不行，因为这周我们人手不够。
origin: 源自旧时赌博，骰子为核心赌具，无骰子即无戏，引申为拒绝、不行。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，语气直接，无褒贬，用于拒绝提议，对熟人或平级使用，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友邀请你今晚一起去看刚上映的科幻电影，但你明天要参加重要的数学期末考试，今晚必须在家复习，没法赴约。例句："I'd love to catch the new sci-fi movie with you tonight, but no dice — I have to study for my math final tomorrow." 翻译：“我很想今晚和你一起去看那部新的科幻电影，但不行——我明天得复习准备数学期末考试。”

definitionCn: 没有未解决的强烈负面情绪或问题。
englishDefinition: No unresolved strong negative emotions/issues.
example: Even though we lost the debate, there are no hard feelings between our team and the opposing side.
exampleTranslation: 虽然我们在辩论中输了，但我们队和对方之间并没有什么芥蒂。
origin: 源自日常口语，指不记仇、无芥蒂，多用于化解矛盾后表达不怀怨怼。
note: 口语化表达，礼貌中性，无褒贬，用于致歉、拒绝或小摩擦后缓和气氛，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你和好朋友组队参加校园篮球比赛，你在最后时刻失误导致队伍输掉了决赛，你正愧疚地向队友道歉。 例句：I know we lost the game because of my mistake, but I hope you have no hard feelings toward me. 翻译：我知道因为我的失误我们输掉了比赛，但我希望你不会对我心存芥蒂。

definitionCn: 没有限制或规则。
englishDefinition: Without restrictions or rules.
example: When the two veteran comedians got on stage for their roast, it was no holds barred, and they joked about each other's most embarrassing career moments without pulling any punches.
exampleTranslation: 当这两位资深喜剧演员上台参加吐槽大会时，现场毫无顾忌，他们毫不留情地拿彼此职业生涯中最尴尬的时刻开玩笑。
origin: 源自摔跤术语，原指无规则限制的摔跤比赛，后泛指不受任何约束。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，中性偏褒，指不受规则限制，可用于描述竞争、谈判等无约束场景。 场景考察：情景：学校辩论社举办年度主题辩论赛，赛前社长宣布本次决赛不设常规的发言时长限制、论点引用范围限制，选手可以自由展开攻防。 例句：The final round of the debate competition was no holds barred, with contestants freely challenging each other's arguments without time limits or citation restrictions. 翻译：这场辩论赛决赛毫无约束，选手们不受时长或引用规则限制，自由地互相质疑论点。

definitionCn: 这不是可以拿来开玩笑的事。
englishDefinition: Not a subject for levity.
example: When your car breaks down on a deserted highway at midnight, it's no laughing matter.
exampleTranslation: 当你的车在午夜时分抛锚在空无一人的高速公路上时，这可不是闹着玩的事。
origin: 源自日常表达，指事态严肃，不可当作玩笑轻率对待。
note: 口语化表达，适用于严肃场合，无褒贬，礼貌中性，用于提醒他人勿对严肃事戏谑。 场景考察：情景：你正在和朋友闲聊，对方开玩笑说自己最近胖了五斤，还笑着说“大不了明天开始不吃晚饭呗”，你知道他最近因为体重飙升已经出现了膝盖疼、睡觉打鼾的问题，医生反复提醒他必须认真控制体重，不能再不当回事，你想严肃地告诉他这件事已经不是能随便开玩笑的小事了。 例句："Gaining that much weight isn't a laughing matter—your doctor warned you it could cause serious joint and sleep problems if you don't take it seriously." 翻译：体重涨这么多可不是闹着玩的——你的医生早就警告过你，要是不认真对待，这会引发严重的关节和睡眠问题。

definitionCn: “他们之间毫无感情可言”这个说法用来形容两个互相厌恶的人之间的关系。 当有人提到另一个人并说“毫无感情可言”时，意思是“我才不会在他/她身上浪费任何感情”。
englishDefinition: 'There's no love lost between them' is used to describe a relationship between two people who dislike each each. When someone refers to someone else and says 'there's no love lost' it means 'I'm not going to waste any love on him/her'.
example: There's no love lost between the two former business partners after their bitter legal battle over the company's assets.
exampleTranslation: 这两位前商业伙伴在就公司资产展开激烈的法律纠纷后，彼此之间毫无好感可言。
origin: 原指不再向对方付出爱意，后引申为两人互相厌恶、毫无好感。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，无褒贬，仅客观描述双方互不喜欢、无好感，不用于正式文书或礼貌夸赞语境。 场景考察：情景：两个性格不合的同班同学，每次小组作业都互相挑刺，见面也从不主动打招呼，彼此都看不顺眼。 例句：There's no love lost between the two classmates who always bicker during group projects. 翻译：这两个同班同学在小组作业时总是吵来吵去，彼此之间毫无好感。

definitionCn: “没有人是一座孤岛”这句话表达了这样一种观点：人类在与他人隔绝时会表现不佳，需要成为社群的一部分才能蓬勃发展。
englishDefinition: The phrase 'no man is an island' expresses the idea that human beings do badly when isolated from others and need to be part of a community in order to thrive.
example: No man is an island, so when you're facing a tough time at work, don't hesitate to reach out to your colleagues for support.
exampleTranslation: 没有人是一座孤岛，所以当你在工作中遇到困难时，不要犹豫向同事寻求支持。
origin: 源自约翰·多恩布道文，喻人非孤立存在，需依托社群方能更好发展。
note: 适用于日常口语或非正式演讲，表中性偏积极，强调互助，勿用于指责他人孤立。 场景考察：情景：你的好朋友刚进入大学，因为性格内向，总喜欢独来独往，不参加社团活动也不和同学交流，最近他跟你抱怨说大学生活很孤单、找不到方向，你打算用这个俚语开导他。 例句：You should join some campus clubs and make more friends; remember that no man is an island, and you'll feel much more supported and fulfilled when you're part of a community. 翻译：你应该加入一些校园社团多交些朋友，记住没有人是一座孤岛，当你成为集体的一份子时，你会感受到更多支持，也会更有成就感。

definitionCn: 蛋糕和美酒是美好生活的代名词，就像啤酒和九柱游戏一样。
englishDefinition: Cakes and ale are synonymous with the good life, like beer and skittles.
example: After years of hard work, he finally got to enjoy the cakes and ale he’d always dreamed of.
exampleTranslation: 经过多年的努力，他终于得以享受自己一直向往的美好生活。
origin: 源自莎士比亚《第十二夜》，喻指世俗享乐，与“啤酒与撞柱戏”同义。
note: 口语化表达，偏中性，用于调侃享乐生活，非正式场合使用，对熟人或轻松语境适用，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：周末家庭聚餐时，奶奶看到你刚吃完一大块奶油蛋糕，又伸手去拿旁边的啤酒杯，笑着问你是不是还想继续享受这些美食与饮品。 例句："No more cakes and ale?" Grandma asked, eyeing my empty dessert plate and the half-full glass of beer. 翻译：“还吃蛋糕、喝啤酒吗？”奶奶看着我空了的甜点盘和半满的啤酒杯问道。

definitionCn: 什么也别说，以免惹祸上身。
englishDefinition: Say nothing and avoid repercussions.
example: When the manager asked who had spilled coffee on the office printer, everyone stayed quiet — no names, no pack-drill.
exampleTranslation: 当经理问是谁把咖啡洒在办公室打印机上时，所有人都保持了沉默——多一事不如少一事，免得惹祸上身。
origin: 源自英军军纪，不告发则免罚，指不声张可避祸。
note: 口语英式俚语，非正式，中性偏自保，用于劝人守口如瓶避祸，勿对长辈或正式场合使用。 场景考察：情景：你在学校走廊里看到两个平时爱打闹的同学偷偷把邻班同学的限量版钢笔藏进了消防柜，对方追问时你不想惹麻烦，也不想被卷进后续的纠纷里。 例句：When the teacher asked who had hidden the classmate's limited-edition pen in the fire cabinet, she decided to stay silent, thinking no names, no pack-drill. 翻译：当老师问是谁把同学的限量版钢笔藏进消防柜时，她决定保持沉默，想着不多嘴就不会惹上麻烦。

definitionCn: 有价值的成果，无论是健康、财富还是成就，都只能通过努力、吃苦或牺牲来获得。
englishDefinition: Worthwhile results, whether fitness, money, or achievement, come only through effort, discomfort, or sacrifice.
example: If you want to master a new language, remember that no pain no gain—consistent daily practice will always pay off.
exampleTranslation: 如果你想掌握一门新语言，记住“没有付出就没有收获”——每天坚持练习总会有回报的。
origin: 源自健身领域，指健身需承受肌肉酸痛的付出，才能收获身材变好的回报。
note: 适用于口语鼓励他人付出，非正式场合，无褒贬，礼貌中性，勿用于正式文书或对长辈生硬说教。 场景考察：情景：你为了准备学校的马拉松比赛，连续三个月每天清晨都早起在操场跑步，哪怕刮风下雨也没有中断训练，最终在比赛中拿到了年级第三名的好成绩。 例句：After months of waking up at 6 a.m. every day to train for the marathon, I finally won third place in my grade — no pain no gain. 翻译：连续几个月每天早上六点起床训练马拉松后，我最终拿到了年级第三名——没有付出就没有收获。

definitionCn: “恶人永无宁日”有其字面含义——即恶人将在地狱中受折磨。
englishDefinition: 'No rest for the wicked has a literal meaning - that the wicked shall be tormented in Hell.
example: After pulling a double shift at the hospital, the exhausted nurse joked, "No rest for the wicked" when her manager asked her to cover one more patient.
exampleTranslation: 在医院连值两个班后，疲惫的护士被经理要求再照看一位病人时，她开玩笑说：“坏人永无宁日啊。”
origin: 源自《圣经》，原指恶人在地狱永受折磨，现泛指人需不停劳作、不得清闲。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，无褒贬，礼貌中性，多用于熟人之间自嘲或调侃需持续忙碌的状态。 场景考察：情景：你周末本来打算在家躺平休息，结果刚起床就接到老板的临时加班通知，你一边收拾电脑一边忍不住吐槽。 例句：I was planning to sleep in this weekend, but no rest for the wicked — my boss just called me in for an emergency meeting. 翻译：我本来打算这个周末睡个懒觉，但恶人永无宁日——我老板刚打电话叫我去开紧急会议。

word: No room to swing a cat
definitionCn: 一个局促狭小的空间。
englishDefinition: An awkwardly small, confined space.
example: My first apartment was so tiny that there was no room to swing a cat, but it was all I could afford at the time.
exampleTranslation: 我的第一套公寓小得转不开身，但那是我当时唯一负担得起的房子。
origin: 源自旧时英国猫刑，指空间狭小到无法挥鞭行刑。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，无褒贬，形容空间极度狭小，勿用于正式文书。 场景考察：情景：周末你和室友挤在刚租的10平米小单间里收拾行李，转身都能碰到对方的胳膊肘。 例句：Our new studio apartment is so tiny that there's no room to swing a cat. 翻译：我们新租的单间公寓太小了，简直连转身的空间都没有。

definitionCn: “没门儿，何塞”是一种断然拒绝的说法，意思是绝对不行或无论如何都不可能。
englishDefinition: No way, Jose is an emphatic refusal, meaning absolutely not or under no circumstances.
example: When my friend asked me to help him move on a Sunday morning after I'd worked a double shift the night before, I told him, "No way, Jose!"
exampleTranslation: 当我朋友让我在前一晚连班之后的周日早上帮他搬家时，我对他说：“绝对不行！”
origin: 源自20世纪美国押头韵俚语，借Jose押韵强化语气，表断然拒绝。
note: 口语化强烈拒绝表达，非正式场合使用，语气随意，无褒贬，适用于熟人或日常轻松交流，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友邀请你在期末考试当天的凌晨三点一起去通宵看露天电影，你第二天还要参加占总成绩40%的高数闭卷考试，完全不可能答应这个离谱的邀约。 例句：No way, Jose, I can't skip my final exam just to watch a movie at 3 a.m. 翻译：绝对不行，我可不能为了凌晨三点去看电影就翘掉期末考试。

definitionCn: 在伦敦东区押韵俚语中，“north and south”指的是人的嘴巴。
englishDefinition: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'north and south' means a person's mouth.
example: He's always got a pie and mash in his north and south whenever we meet up.
exampleTranslation: 我们每次见面的时候，他嘴里总塞着馅饼和土豆泥。
origin: 源自伦敦考克尼押韵俚语，以“north and south”押韵指代人的嘴巴。
note: 考克尼俚语，非正式口语，无褒贬，指嘴，仅用于伦敦东区方言圈，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：在伦敦东区的酒吧里，一位老派的伦敦人看到朋友只顾闷头喝酒、一句话也不说，便用手肘碰了碰对方，打趣道："Hey, use your north and south and tell me how you really feel about the new landlord!" 例句：My grandad always tells me to shut my north and south when I'm being cheeky at the dinner table. 翻译：我爷爷总在我吃饭时调皮捣蛋的时候叫我闭嘴。

definitionCn: “爱打听闲事的人”（有时也拼作 nosey parker）指的是过分好奇、爱管闲事的人。
englishDefinition: A 'nosy parker', sometimes spelled 'nosey parker', is a person of an overly inquisitive or prying nature.
example: My nosy neighbor keeps peeking through my curtains to see what I'm doing.
exampleTranslation: 我那个爱管闲事的邻居总是透过我的窗帘偷看我在做什么。
origin: 源自19世纪英国，指爱打听闲事的人，典故与公园中爱窥探的人相关。
note: 口语俚语，带贬义，指爱打听闲事的人，非正式场合使用，对熟人调侃或背后议论，不宜当面称人。 场景考察：情景：周末你正坐在小区楼下的长椅上拆刚收到的快递，邻居王阿姨凑过来盯着你手里的包裹，还不停问你买了什么、花了多少钱、是不是给家里孩子带的礼物，你觉得她实在太爱打听别人的私事了。 例句：My nosy parker neighbor always asks about my private life when she runs into me. 翻译：我那个爱管闲事的邻居每次碰到我，总爱打听我的私生活。

definitionCn: 一声不吭；一言不发。
englishDefinition: Not a sound; not an utterance.
example: When the teacher asked who had broken the classroom window, there was not a dicky-bird from any of the students.
exampleTranslation: 当老师问是谁打破了教室窗户时，没有一个学生吭声。
origin: 源自伦敦俚语，dicky-bird谐音word，喻指一言不发、毫无声响。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，无褒贬，指毫无声响，多用于日常闲聊，不宜用于正式文书或庄重场合。 场景考察：情景：你参加一场安静的读书会，所有人都在低头专注看书，没人开口说话。 例句：When the teacher asked who had broken the window, there was not a dicky-bird from any of the children in the class. 翻译：当老师问是谁打破了窗户时，班上的孩子们全都一声不吭。

definitionCn: 完全不是；与事实相去甚远。当某事物与预期目标相差甚远时，可用此表达来加强语气。例如，“10万英镑在伦敦买一套房子是不够的——远远不够。”
englishDefinition: Not by any means; a good distance away from being true. It is used for emphasis when something a described as being far from its mark. For example, "£100,000 isn't enough to buy a house in London - not by a long chalk".
example: You might think I'm upset about losing the game, but I'm not by a long chalk.
exampleTranslation: 你可能觉得我输了比赛会很沮丧，但我才没有呢。
origin: 源自旧时用粉笔划线标记距离，表“远非如此、差得远”，用于强调某事远未达标。
note: 口语俚语，表强烈否定，语气随意，无褒贬，适用于非正式场合，对熟人使用，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友问你是不是已经把期末论文写完了，而你其实才刚列好大纲，一个字都还没动笔。 例句："Have you finished your final essay?" "Not by a long chalk—I've only just started outlining it." 翻译：“你期末论文写完了吗？”“差得远呢——我才刚开始列大纲。”

definitionCn: 完全不是；与事实相差甚远。当描述某事物远未达到目标时，可用该短语来加强语气。例如：“10万美元根本不够在纽约买一套房子——远远不够。”
englishDefinition: Not by any means; a good distance away from being true. It is used for emphasis when something a described as being far from its mark. For example, "$100,000 isn't enough to buy a house in New York - not by a long shot".
example: When asked if she had finished the 10,000-word research paper, she admitted she hadn't completed it by a long shot.
exampleTranslation: 当被问及是否写完了那篇一万字的研究论文时，她承认自己远远没有完成。
origin: 源自射击运动，指离命中目标差得远，用于强调某事远非属实。
note: 口语俚语，非正式场合使用，语气随意，无褒贬，表强烈否定，适用于熟人交流，勿用于正式文书或严肃对话。 场景考察：情景：朋友问你是不是已经完成了期末论文，你其实才刚列好大纲，离写完还差很远。 例句："Have you finished your final paper?" "Finished? Not by a long shot—I've only just outlined it." 翻译：“你写完期末论文了吗？”“写完？差得远呢——我才刚列好大纲。”

word: Not for all the tea in China
phonetic: /nɒt fɔː ɔːl ðə tiː ɪn ˈtʃaɪnə/
definitionCn: 无论付出什么代价都不行。
englishDefinition: Not at any price.
example: I wouldn't tell him the secret for all the tea in China.
exampleTranslation: 我绝不会把这个秘密告诉他，无论他出多高的价钱。
origin: 源自19世纪英国对华茶叶贸易，形容即便倾尽中国茶叶财富，也绝不妥协。
note: 口语化表达，礼貌中性，带坚决否定语气，适用于日常非正式交流，不适合正式文书或严肃谈判场合。 场景考察：情景：你的朋友开出了远超市场价的高价，想让你把从小陪伴你长大的、承载着无数童年回忆的老吉他卖给他，你坚决拒绝了这个提议。 例句：I wouldn't sell my old guitar, not for all the tea in China. 翻译：我绝不会卖掉我的旧吉他，无论对方出多高的价钱都不行。

word: Not playing with a full deck
definitionCn: “脑子不太灵光”可以用来形容被认为愚蠢的人。
englishDefinition: 'Not playing with a full deck' might be said about someone who was considered stupid.
example: Don't mind his strange ideas; I think he's not playing with a full deck.
exampleTranslation: 别在意他那些奇怪的想法，我觉得他脑子不太正常。
origin: 源自纸牌游戏，指玩家牌组不全，喻人智力不足、行事糊涂。
note: 口语俚语，带贬义，指人愚笨、神志不清，仅用于非正式场合，勿当面使用，避免冒犯他人。 场景考察：情景：你在咖啡馆听到一位顾客对着咖啡机大喊大叫，因为他坚持认为咖啡机“故意”把他的咖啡变成了液体，还要求经理惩罚这台机器。 例句：When my uncle starts arguing with houseplants about who left the fridge open, everyone agrees he's not playing with a full deck. 翻译：当我叔叔开始和室内盆栽争论是谁没关冰箱时，所有人都觉得他脑子不太正常。

definitionCn: 这是拿破仑·波拿巴拒绝与约瑟芬皇后发生关系时据称作出的回应。
englishDefinition: This is the supposed response by Napoleon Bonaparte when declining sex with Empress Joséphine.
example: When his partner teased him about being too tired for intimacy after a long work trip, he joked, "Not tonight, Joséphine," and rolled over to get some rest.
exampleTranslation: 当他的伴侣调侃他长途出差后太累没法亲热时，他开玩笑说“今晚不行，约瑟芬”，然后翻身休息去了。
origin: 源自拿破仑拒绝与约瑟芬皇后同房的传闻，后喻指委婉拒绝亲密邀约。
note: 非正式口语，婉拒亲密邀约的戏谑表达，带调侃意味，仅适用于熟人玩笑，正式场合慎用。 场景考察：情景：周末晚上，你刚结束连续三天的高强度项目加班，回到家只想瘫在沙发上看喜欢的纪录片，伴侣兴致勃勃地提议今晚一起做点浪漫的事，你温柔又疲惫地婉拒。 例句：After pulling three all-nighters to finish the product launch, I told my partner "Not tonight Joséphine" and curled up on the couch with a warm blanket to watch my favorite show. 翻译：连续熬了三个通宵完成产品发布后，我对伴侣说“今晚不行，约瑟芬”，裹着暖乎乎的毯子蜷在沙发上看我最爱的节目。

definitionCn: 毫无价值。
englishDefinition: Worthless.
example: After the company's scandal broke, its once highly sought-after stock became not worth a plugged nickel, and no investor was willing to touch it.
exampleTranslation: 在这家公司的丑闻曝光后，它曾经备受追捧的股票变得一文不值，没有投资者愿意碰它。
origin: 旧时指劣币，镍币被打孔塞物后价值极低，喻毫无价值。
